articles.title: Apple encerra pregão avaliada em US$ 5 trilhões pela primeira vez | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresa se isola como a segunda mais valiosa do mundo, atrás apenas da Nvidia.
articles.summary: Empresa se isola como a segunda mais valiosa do mundo, atrás apenas da Nvidia.
articles.body:
Modelos da linha iPhone 17 em loja da Apple nos EUA, em foto de 19 de setembro de 2025 — Foto: Reuters/Shannon Stapleton

A Apple encerrou o pregão desta quarta-feira (14) com alta de 0,5% em suas ações e registrou valor de mercado acima dos US$ 5 trilhões (cerca de R$ 25 trilhões) pela primeira vez em sua história.

A empresa já tinha alcançado esse valor durante o pregão , quando chegou a se tornar a marca mais valiosa do mundo por alguns instantes.

Com o valor alcançado nesta quarta, a Apple se isolou como a segunda empresa mais valiosa do mundo e a segunda a ter alcançado este valor de mercado no fechamento do pregão.

A primeira foi a fabricante de semicondutores Nvidia, que chegou a esta marca em outubro de 2025 e agora caminha para ser avaliada em US$ 6 trilhões (R$ 30 trilhões) .

As ações da Apple tem se valorizado em meio à demanda elevada por produtos como o iPhone e os computadores Mac mini e iMac, que passaram a estar disponíveis nos Estados Unidos por meio de programas de assinatura.

Em setembro, a empresa lançou novas versões do iPhone , incluindo uma com tela dobrável , além de novos fones de ouvido e relógios inteligentes. Os preços no Brasil chegam a R$ 30.999.

A Apple passa por uma mudança na gestão que envolve a saída de Tim Cook após 15 anos como CEO e a chegada de John Ternus , que era vice-presidente sênior de Engenharia de Hardware na empresa.

Ternus planeja realizar uma reformulação para dar mais foco à engenharia, lançar produtos com mais frequência e tornar a estrutura da companhia mais enxuta, revelou a Bloomberg no final de setembro.

Entre as mudanças, estão a mudança do tradicional calendário de lançamentos de produtos, que hoje é concentrado em setembro, e a redução de cargos de gerência intermediária.

Segundo a reportagem, Ternus sinalizou internamente que a Apple deve lançar produtos com mais rapidez e testar novas ideias para se manter competitiva na era da inteligência artificial.

articles.title: Upfront Globo 2027 apresenta principais novidades para o próximo ano | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento teve anúncios sobre a Copa do Mundo Feminina, o BBB 27, entretenimento e publicidade, além do retorno de 'Avenida Brasil'.
articles.summary: Evento teve anúncios sobre a Copa do Mundo Feminina, o BBB 27, entretenimento e publicidade, além do retorno de 'Avenida Brasil'.
articles.body:
O Upfront Globo 2027 , um dos eventos mais aguardados do calendário da indústria criativa brasileira, foi realizado na noite desta quarta-feira (14), no Auditório Ibirapuera, em São Paulo.

O evento apresentou ao mercado as oportunidades de mídia da Globo para o próximo ano. A partir dele, anunciantes e agências podem planejar e garantir espaços nos principais produtos e projetos da empresa, tanto nacionais quanto regionais.

Na abertura da cerimônia, Paulo Marinho, diretor-presidente da Globo, ressaltou que o papel da empresa é criar pontes para que os negócios cheguem à casa e à vida de cada brasileiro todos os dias.

"Essa presença pode se tornar um vínculo duradouro. E esse é o convite que fazemos a vocês", afirmou.

Upfront Globo 2027 — Foto: Maurício Fidalgo/Globo

"A relevância da Globo está ligada a esses compromissos e a um encontro entre quem investe, quem informa, quem cria e quem vive as nossas histórias. É para isso que seguimos construindo a Globo junto com todos vocês", acrescentou Marinho.

Manzar Feres, diretora-geral de Negócios em Publicidade da Globo, destacou a capacidade da empresa de reunir e mobilizar pessoas e, a partir disso, gerar valor para as marcas.

Para ela, influência vai além do alcance e passa também por fazer uma mensagem importar, ser percebida, lembrada e capaz de mover pessoas.

“A Globo tem uma combinação muito particular de forças para fazer isso acontecer. (...) Neste ano, nós já falamos com quase 200 milhões de pessoas. Só até setembro, foram mais de 4 trilhões de minutos consumidos em nossas plataformas”, afirmou.

“Alcançar, a gente sabe que é só o começo. Importa também o que acontece depois. Na Globo, uma história não termina quando o programa acaba. Ela continua reverberando, influencia conversas e vira negócio”, acrescentou.

O Upfront 2027 teve início com o cantor Péricles, que levantou o público ao som de "A Gente Bota pra Quebrar". Veja os destaques abaixo.

Upfront 2027: Luís Roberto, Renata Silveira, Ana Thaís Matos, Mari Spinelli e Luana Maluf subiram ao palco para receber as jogadoras e o técnico da Seleção Brasileira, Arthur Elias, para falar sobre a Copa do Mundo Feminina de 2027. — Foto: Maurício Fidalgo/Globo

Luís Roberto, Renata Silveira, Ana Thaís Matos, Mari Spinelli e Luana Maluf receberam Arthur Elias, técnico da Seleção Brasileira, e as jogadoras convocadas para falar sobre a Copa do Mundo Feminina de 2027.

O encontro destacou a expectativa para o Mundial, que será realizado no Brasil e promete mobilizar torcedores de todo o país. O Troféu da Copa do Mundo da FIFA também desembarcou no país e chegou ao palco do Upfront.

Além da grande cobertura do evento esportivo, a Globo apresentou conteúdos que levarão o Mundial para além dos campos.

No GNT, Sabrina Sato comanda um esquenta com encontros que trazem histórias das atletas antes do início dos jogos. No Multishow, Blogueirinha acompanha os bastidores do Mundial em um mockumentary com muito humor.

Ainda durante o evento, Sabrina Sato levou a atriz Alice Carvalho ao palco do Upfront 2027 para apresentar "Marta", cinebiografia da maior jogadora da história do futebol feminino mundial.

Dirigido por Andrucha Waddington, o filme traz Alice Carvalho no papel da protagonista, em um elenco que reúne Drica Moraes, Irandhir Santos, Thelmo Fernandes e Claudia Di Moura. "Marta" chega aos cinemas brasileiros em abril de 2027.

Em 2027, a Globo também reúne um portfólio de transmissões que acompanha os principais acontecimentos esportivos do ano , com cobertura multiplataforma, informação e entretenimento para diferentes públicos.

Tadeu Schmidt apresenta o BBB 27 — Foto: Maurício Fidalgo/Globo

Tadeu Schmidt apresentou as novidades do BBB 27 . A próxima temporada reúne veteranos, pipocas e camarotes e amplia a participação do público com novas dinâmicas, um "Sincerão" mais ágil e uma Casa de Vidro que definirá parte do elenco e dará vantagens no jogo.

"Nosso 'Sincerão' está reformulado, mais dinâmico, gameficado. Está diferente. Vocês vão gostar", afirmou o apresentador Tadeu Schmidt.

Na TV Globo , a eliminação de terça-feira será seguida por uma conversa do eliminado com um fã e um hater, enquanto os domingos terão duas edições : uma à tarde, com o início da formação do paredão, e outra à noite, com a conclusão da dinâmica.

Chef de Alto Nível — Foto: Fábio Rocha/Globo

Em um vídeo, Ana Maria Braga e os chefs Alex Atala, Jefferson Rueda e Renata Vanzetto confirmaram no Upfront a terceira temporada de Chef de Alto Nível para 2027.

A renovação vem após o sucesso comercial da atual edição, que teve todas as cotas de patrocínio vendidas.

Rafaella Justus, Ticiane Pinheiro e Helô Pinheiro — Foto: Maurício Fidalgo/Globo

Ticiane Pinheiro subiu ao palco acompanhada da mãe, Helô Pinheiro, e da filha, Rafaella Justus, para apresentar "Academia dos Nepo Babies", novo reality show Original Globoplay , produzido pelos Estúdios Globo .

Na competição, filhos de personalidades brasileiras precisam testar novas habilidades em profissões inusitadas.

César Tralli e Maju Coutinho — Foto: Maurício Fidalgo/Globo

Maju Coutinho e César Tralli ressaltaram que, em 2027, o Jornalismo da Globo reafirma o compromisso com a informação bem apurada, ágil e próxima do público , sempre presente onde os fatos acontecem e dedicada a explicá-los com clareza, profundidade e relevância.

Ana Clara — Foto: Maurício Fidalgo/Globo

No Upfront , Ana Clara anunciou que a Globo prepara um novo reality de relacionamento que irá explorar os desafios, expectativas e dinâmicas que surgem quando se decide casar.

Ainda sem apresentador definido, o programa tem estreia prevista para 2027.

Cauã Reymond — Foto: Maurício Fidalgo/Globo

Cauã Reymond apresentou o Welcome Ads , novo formato publicitário do Globoplay exibido na tela de login, antes da escolha do perfil e do conteúdo.

A novidade oferece às marcas um novo ponto de contato, em um momento de grande visibilidade no início da navegação.

O Welcome Ads integra a evolução da oferta comercial do Globoplay e se soma a soluções como Pause Ads, Binge Ads e inserção dinâmica de publicidade no simulcast dos canais lineares.

Marcos Mion, Serginho Groisman, Daniel, Louro Mané, Luciano Huck, Patrícia Poeta, Maria Beltrão e Eliana — Foto: Maurício Fidalgo/Globo

Luciano Huck, Serginho Groisman, Marcos Mion, Maria Beltrão, Patrícia Poeta, Eliana, Daniel e Louro Mané destacaram a força e a diversidade do entretenimento da Globo, com atrações que acompanham o público em diferentes momentos e plataformas.

A atração inédita "Chefinho de Alto Nível" foi anunciada pela Eliana. A novidade leva o universo da gastronomia para o público infantil ao "Em Família com Eliana".

No mesmo palco, Luciano Huck anunciou um reforço no time de entretenimento da Globo em 2027: Márcio Garcia , que vai apresentar um game show desenvolvido pelos Estúdios Globo em parceria com a Endemol Shine Brasil, com provas cocriadas com marcas.

Parte do elenco de Avenida Brasil 2 — Foto: Maurício Fidalgo/Globo

Um dos principais anúncios da noite transformou o palco do Upfront 2027 em um reencontro marcado pela emoção.

Adriana Esteves, Murilo Benício, Débora Falabella, Cauã Reymond, Eliane Giardini, Marcos Caruso, Leticia Isnard, Thalita Carauta e Karol Lannes se reuniram para confirmar o retorno de "Avenida Brasil". A nova história também recebe nomes como Mel Maia, Thomas Aquino e Jessica Ellen.

Mais de uma década depois de conquistar o país, a novela que marcou uma geração volta a abrir as portas do Divino e promete fazer o Brasil parar mais uma vez.

articles.title: Car payments just hit a record $787 a month—and 1 in 4 new-car buyers is now signing a 7-year loan
articles.summary: New-car payments, loan sizes and lifetime interest all set records last quarter, even with rates flat at 7%. Six-figure households are still buying. Everyone...
articles.body:
American drivers face a daunting market. The average monthly payment on a financed new car hit a record $787 in the third quarter, according to Edmunds , up from $777 in the second quarter and $756 a year earlier.

Buyers are also borrowing more than ever. The average amount financed climbed to a record $44,664, while the average new vehicle sold for $50,562 in September, per Kelley Blue Book , just $52 shy of the all-time high. Nationwide, auto loan balances reached $1.71 trillion in the second quarter, according to the New York Fed , roughly 56% more than a decade earlier .

For Joseph Yoon, consumer insights analyst at Edmunds, the math is brutally simple: Vehicle prices sit near record highs, and interest rates remain stubbornly elevated, with the average new-car APR holding at 7%.

"Mix those things together and then you get record-high monthly payments," Yoon told Fortune . "Just how the math works out."

The road that led to record car payments

So how exactly did we arrive here? Yoon points to the pandemic as a significant precursor to the state of car sales. When factories shut down and parts ran short, manufacturers faced a choice: build fewer cars, or build the ones with higher margins. They chose the latter.

"Automakers realize, 'Hey, even if we lose a couple million units across the board, if we have high margins, our profits look great,'" Yoon said. "And that's perfectly fine. But as consumers, we drew the short straw, and have to pay for elevated prices."

The result: New vehicles now cost about 30% more than they did six years ago, as Fortune has reported .

For buyers struggling to afford today's prices, the dealership finance office offers a tempting solution: stretch the loan.

Indeed, a record share of new-car buyers decided that a seven-year loan sounded less scary than the alternative. In the third quarter, 25.5% of financed new-car purchases carried terms of 84 months or more, according to Edmunds , up from 23.9% the prior quarter and 21.8% a year earlier. Even so, a record 21.2% of buyers committed to monthly payments of $1,000 or more.

But longer terms carry consequences, some of which aren't immediately obvious.

"The longer you have a loan term, technically the longer you're paying just toward interest, not toward the principal of the loan, especially when the interest rates are so high," Yoon said.

The average amount of interest paid over the life of a new-car loan reached a record $9,938 in the third quarter, up from $9,442 a year earlier, Edmunds found. That increase came even though rates didn't budge; Edmunds attributed it to buyers financing larger amounts over longer periods.

articles.title: Data center builder offers Kansas town residents $10,000
articles.summary: Digital Realty is offering utility and property tax credits to residents of De Soto, Kansas, in a bid to win public support for a data center facility.
articles.body:
Amid a pronounced public backlash against data center construction in the U.S., one real estate developer is making an offer it hopes will win over one Kansas community: money.

Digital Realty is offering every household in De Soto, Kansas, where it plans to build a data center, $1,000 in utility and property tax credits for 10 years.

"Digital Realty builds critical infrastructure that enables the modern economy, and we believe we also have a responsibility to help strengthen the communities that make this growth possible," Andy Power, the developer's president and CEO, said in a statement on Wednesday.

The offer is part of a $20 million community investment Digital Realty is pledging in De Soto as the company paves the way for a 280-acre data center site. The company said the project, which will eventually cover 1,400 acres, will provide recurring tax revenue, create jobs and deliver other economic benefits to local residents.

Digital Realty, a publicly traded company based in Austin, Texas, with a market worth of more than $67 billion, said in a news release that it is working with De Soto to finalize distribution of the $1,000 credits to households.

The company, whose clients include Amazon Web Services , Microsoft and Nvidia, expects to create 250 permanent jobs for local suppliers and contractors once the site is complete. The initial phase of development will also support "thousands of construction jobs over time," Digital Realty said in its news release.

A recent CBS News poll found that more Americans oppose than favor building a new data center in their area, citing concerns that the facilities harm the environment, drain local resources and raise utility costs.

articles.title: Oil prices gain on attacks in Saudi Arabia, Iran's new tactics to target tankers
articles.summary: By Nicole Jao NEW YORK, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Oil prices rose on Wednesday after the Houthis attacked Saudi Aramco's headquarters and Iran said it was deploying...
articles.body:
NEW YORK, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Oil prices rose on Wednesday after the Houthis attacked Saudi Aramco's headquarters and Iran said it was deploying new tactics to target ships and keep oil prices high.

Brent crude futures settled up ‌37 cents, or 0.35%, at $106.06 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 95 cents, or 1.01%, to $95.09, a three-week ‌high.

Attacks on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and strikes between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-allied Houthis are driving up oil prices, said Phil Flynn, senior analyst ​with the Price Futures Group.

"We're seeing a lot of fear trade today," Flynn added.

Iranian officials declined to provide details of the new strategy to target ships, but one said Iran started using different offensive tactics about 10 days ago.

Gulf oil flows excluding Iran surged in September to more than 81% of prewar levels, data showed, led by a recovery in Saudi exports. Iranian exports fell to zero owing to a US blockade.

"More crude ‌reaching international markets does not necessarily mean more ⁠oil is being produced," Saxo Bank analyst Ole Hansen said in a note. "Some of the recovery reflects a redistribution of available barrels, including volumes that would otherwise have supplied regional refineries."

The Houthis attacked ⁠an administrative building belonging to state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco in the city of Dhahran, causing a limited fire, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said.

The group has fired ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia over the past week in what it says is retaliation for the kingdom's support of ​Yemeni ​government forces. Riyadh's international airport has been hit four times, with a strike ​on Saturday killing 13 people.

Meanwhile, a container ship sank ‌in waters south of the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a naval mine and catching fire, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said in a statement shared by state media on Wednesday. This was a day after the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said a container ship and a tanker were hit by unknown projectiles in the strait.

"The expectation that increased Russian diesel exports will ease market tightness is likely to limit sharp price movement in either direction," said Hiroyuki Kikukawa, chief strategist at Nissan Securities Investment.

US President Donald Trump announced on Friday ‌that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets and his ​administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian diesel that were designed to deprive Moscow ​of revenue for its war on Ukraine.

articles.title: Bolsa Família não teve reajuste maior que acumulado do salário mínimo  | G1
articles.standfirst: Publicação diz: 'Governo dá mais de 15% de aumento para quem não trabalha e apenas 6% para quem trabalha?'. Mas post omite que Bolsa Família não tinha correção desde março de 2023; e, nesse mesmo período, alta do salário mínimo foi de 22,8%; entenda.
articles.summary: Ao Fato ou Fake, Ministério do Planejamento informou que o salário mínimo subiu 22,8% no mesmo período.
articles.body:
Bolsa Família não teve reajuste maior que salário mínimo nos últimos 3 anos — Foto: g1

Circulam nas redes sociais publicações alegando que o governo Lula ( PT ) deu mais de 15% de reajuste para o Bolsa Família, mas corrigiu em apenas 6% o salário mínimo. #NÃOÉBEMASSIM .

Selo Não é Bem Assim (Horizontal) — Foto: g1

Publicações que viralizaram no X e no Instagram desde o final de setembro exibem uma imagem do presidente Lula (PT) segurando um cartão do programa social Bolsa Família. Abaixo, há o seguinte texto: "Discurso que gera polêmica: 'Como um partido que se diz dos trabalhadores dá mais de 15% de aumento para quem não trabalha e apenas 6% para quem trabalha?', diz trabalhador CLT".

Veja um exemplo de legenda que acompanha a imagem: "Em um vídeo que acumula milhares de visualizações, um trabalhador regido pela CLT fez um desabafo direto sobre a condução econômica do governo: Como um partido que se diz dos trabalhadores dá mais de 15% de aumento para quem não trabalha e apenas 6% para quem trabalha? O questionamento expõe a insatisfação da classe trabalhadora com a perda do poder de compra e com o ritmo dos reajustes salariais frente aos repasses de programas assistenciais".

Mas esses enunciados omitem que o reajuste anterior do Bolsa Família havia ocorrido em 2023. E que, nesse mesmo período, o salário mínimo acumulou um aumento de 22,8% . Em 2024, o valor passou de R$ 1.320 para R$ 1.412 . Em 2025, chegou a R$ 1.518 . E, em 2026, subiu para R$ 1.621 . O percentual de 6%, citado nos posts desta checagem, é próximo apenas do registrado na correção mais recente: 6,8% (de R$ 1.518 para R$ 1.621) – leia detalhes abaixo .

Em 17 de setembro, a 17 dias do primeiro turno da corrida presidencial, o governo federal anunciou o reajuste dos benefícios do Bolsa Família em 15% . Com isso, o piso do programa de R$ 600 para R$ 691. Já o benefício médio subirá dos atuais R$ 675 para R$ 777, informou o Ministério do Planejamento. O primeiro repasse com os novos valores está previsto para 19 de outubro .

À época do anúncio do aumento para o Bolsa Família, o governo negou motivação eleitoral e afirmou que a medida recompõe parte da perda do poder de compra causada pela inflação desde o aumento anterior, três anos atrás. De acordo com dados do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), o Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor (INPC) acumulado entre março de 2023 e agosto de 2026 foi de 15,04%.

Economistas e especialistas consultados pelo g1 questionaram o momento da alteração e o risco às contas públicas .

Procurado pelo Fato ou Fake , o Ministério do Planjeamento e Orçamento disse, por e-mail: "A recomposição de 15% do benefício Bolsa Família corresponde a correção dos valores pela variação inflacionária acumulada do Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor (INPC) entre março de 2023 e agosto de 2026, um período de 3 anos em que não houve reajuste. Isso não ocorreu com o salário mínimo, que manteve valorização real nos últimos 3 anos" .

O Fato ou Fake consultou o economista Carlos Eduardo Oliveira Jr, do Conselheiro Conselho Regional de Economia de São Paulo (Corecon-SP), que explicou: "Para uma comparação adequada, o ideal é analisar a evolução acumulada do salário mínimo e do Bolsa Família entre 2023 e 2026, e não comparar o reajuste anual do mínimo com a recomposição acumulada de 15,04% aplicada ao programa social. Nesse critério, o salário mínimo teve um avanço de 22,8%, contra 15,04% do Bolsa Família" .

articles.title: Iowa: água poluída e câncer pautam eleição no coração do agro dos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Temas geram tensão entre moradores dos centros urbanos e produtores rurais do estado. País terá eleições de meio de mandato no início de novembro, que vão renovar Câmara e cerca de um terço do Senado.
articles.summary: Estado tem a segunda maior taxa de novos diagnósticos de câncer dos EUA.
articles.body:
Um riacho atravessa uma área de cultivo em Marshalltown, em Iowa. — Foto: Brittany Peterson/AP

O estado de Iowa, uma das potências do agronegócio dos Estados Unidos, enfrenta um déficit orçamentário, custos elevados e dificuldades econômicas provocadas por disputas comerciais que têm pressionado os agricultores.

Mas dois problemas que se arrastam há décadas — a qualidade da água e os índices de câncer — ganharam destaque nas campanhas para as eleições de meio de mandato, conhecidas como midterms.

➡️ As midterms são realizadas na metade do mandato presidencial. Elas renovam toda a Câmara dos Representantes e cerca de um terço do Senado, além de definir governadores e outros cargos estaduais e locais.

Em Iowa, esses temas polêmicos estão sendo abordados em debates, mesas-redondas e propagandas eleitorais de candidatos democratas e republicanos a diferentes cargos.

Historicamente, o assunto tem sido um tabu político para evitar apontar responsabilidades da indústria agropecuária de Iowa, um dos principais produtores de milho, soja e suínos dos Estados Unidos.

➡️ Os fertilizantes químicos e os dejetos animais usados na produção agropecuária, por exemplo, contêm nitratos e fósforo, que podem ser levados pela água da chuva ou do derretimento da neve até os rios do estado.

O problema há muito tempo provoca tensões entre os centros urbanos de Iowa, de tendência mais progressista e que dependem de rios e lagos para o abastecimento de água potável, e os produtores rurais, em sua maioria conservadores.

Cada vez mais agricultores adotam práticas para impedir que esses resíduos sejam levados para os cursos d’água, embora críticos afirmem que a falta de regulamentação obriga os moradores que vivem rio abaixo a pagar pela poluição.

A atenção ao tema aumentou — e o cálculo político mudou — após dois anos consecutivos de restrições ao uso da água na região de Des Moines, somados ao crescimento do movimento “Make America Healthy Again” (“Tornar os Estados Unidos saudáveis novamente”) nas pequenas cidades e comunidades rurais de Iowa.

Índices de câncer são um problema crescente em Iowa

Iowa tem a segunda maior taxa de novos diagnósticos de câncer do país. Os diagnósticos de alguns tipos, como os de próstata, mama e pulmão, estão aumentando mais rapidamente no estado do que nos Estados Unidos como um todo. O problema afeta tanto as áreas urbanas quanto as rurais.

Uma nova pesquisa da Universidade de Iowa, financiada pelo governo estadual, mostra que fatores demográficos e comportamentais, como o tabagismo e o consumo excessivo de álcool em uma única ocasião, podem explicar a maior parte — mas não a totalidade — da incidência acima do normal de cinco tipos de câncer no estado.

Na próxima etapa, os pesquisadores avaliarão fatores ambientais, incluindo os níveis de nitrato.

“O verdadeiro problema é a água e os nitratos”, disse o democrata Josh Turek, candidato ao Senado dos Estados Unidos, durante uma conversa com pacientes com câncer na semana passada. “Todo morador de Iowa merece ter a certeza, ao abrir a torneira, de que sua água está limpa e não está lhe causando câncer.”

Alguns estudos encontraram uma associação entre nitratos na água potável e determinadas doenças, mas o tema continua em debate. A Agência de Proteção Ambiental dos Estados Unidos (EPA) atualmente não classifica os nitratos como um fator de risco para o câncer.

A agência iniciou um plano para rever essa avaliação em 2017, mas o processo foi paralisado, retomado e novamente interrompido sob diferentes governos na Casa Branca.

A deputada federal republicana Ashley Hinson, que disputa a vaga com Turek, reuniu recentemente agricultores, pesquisadores e autoridades locais para discutir os problemas da água em Iowa.

Ela afirmou que é preciso manter os investimentos em infraestrutura, monitoramento da qualidade da água e programas de conservação para garantir água potável segura à população. Também disse que as pessoas podem se sentir seguras porque a água tratada que chega às torneiras atende às normas federais.

“Todos sabemos que temos alguns desafios aqui em Iowa”, afirmou. “Não acho que a qualidade da água seja uma questão partidária.”

Há mais de dez anos, a companhia de abastecimento de água da região de Des Moines entrou na Justiça para que outras administrações locais ajudassem a pagar pela remoção de nitratos da água, que custava cerca de US$ 16 mil por dia.

Essas regiões ficam em trechos dos rios anteriores à chegada da água a Des Moines. A ação foi rejeitada, e líderes republicanos de Iowa comemoraram a decisão.

No ano passado, a Central Iowa Water Works proibiu os moradores de regar gramados pela primeira vez, para diminuir o consumo de água e aliviar a sobrecarga do sistema de remoção de nitratos. Políticos do estado rejeitaram tentativas de responsabilizar os agricultores.

Nos últimos anos, Iowa vinha investindo quase US$ 100 milhões por ano em medidas para reduzir a presença de nutrientes na água.

Em maio, a governadora republicana Kim Reynolds e parlamentares destinaram mais US$ 320 milhões a obras de infraestrutura hídrica, incentivos à conservação ambiental e outros projetos. Parte dos recursos foi reservada à modernização dos equipamentos da Central Iowa Water Works.

“A qualidade da água não é uma questão do campo. Não é uma questão das cidades, nem uma questão política”, disse Reynolds. “Mas é absolutamente inegociável.”

Apesar dos investimentos, a demora nos resultados continua sendo alvo de críticas, inclusive dos candidatos que disputam a sucessão da governadora.

Tema ganha destaque na disputa pelo governo

O republicano Zach Lahn e o democrata Rob Sand defendem que o estado dê mais atenção à qualidade da água. Nenhum dos dois, porém, propõe obrigar os produtores rurais a adotar práticas que reduzam a quantidade de poluentes levados das lavouras e criações para os rios.

Lahn recebeu o apoio do comitê político MAHA Action no início da disputa interna do partido. Diferentemente de muitos colegas republicanos, ele associa diretamente a água poluída e os produtos químicos usados na agricultura aos altos índices de câncer em Iowa.

Em agosto, durante um encontro do candidato com eleitores para discutir agricultura no nordeste do estado, uma participante demonstrou preocupação.

Lahn reconheceu a importância de determinados produtos químicos para a produção agrícola.

“Não estamos aqui para proibir produtos”, afirmou, “mas precisamos enfrentar o problema da qualidade da água”.

Nos Estados Unidos, as normas federais permitem até 10 miligramas de nitrato por litro de água potável. O limite foi definido para prevenir a chamada síndrome do bebê azul, condição em que o sangue do bebê não tem oxigênio suficiente. Estudos científicos vêm investigando, porém, se concentrações abaixo desse limite também podem estar associadas a certos tipos de câncer.

Lahn contou que testou a água de seu poço e de um riacho na zona rural do centro-leste de Iowa. Nos dois casos, os níveis de nitrato ficaram muito acima do permitido.

Neste ano, a Central Iowa Water Works precisou manter o sistema de remoção de nitratos funcionando por 193 dias seguidos, um recorde. No auge do verão, mesmo após o tratamento, a água tinha entre oito e nove miligramas de nitrato por litro, perto do limite federal.

Sand também costuma falar da qualidade da água logo no início de seus discursos de campanha. Ele conta que a defesa da água limpa foi um dos motivos que o levaram a se filiar ao Partido Democrata, já que gosta de pescar.

Na terça-feira, após se reunir com sobreviventes de câncer e pais de crianças com a doença, o candidato disse que a preocupação da população com o tema tem crescido nos últimos anos.

“Ouço com frequência pessoas tão preocupadas com isso que se perguntam se querem continuar em Iowa”, disse Sand.

Disputa pela Secretaria de Agricultura de Iowa expõe a tensão

O pesquisador Chris Jones conta que, há 20 anos, informava seu chefe na companhia de abastecimento de água de Des Moines sobre os níveis de nitrato nos rios.

“Ele me perguntava: ‘Cadê a indignação?’”, lembrou Jones. “Agora, a indignação chegou.”

Jones, que depois trabalhou no monitoramento da qualidade da água na Universidade de Iowa, considera uma grave falha do estado que os moradores já não confiem na água que bebem.

Pelo Partido Democrata, ele disputa o cargo de secretário de Agricultura de Iowa, escolhido por eleição, e tenta derrotar o atual ocupante, o republicano Mike Naig.

Uma das principais diferenças entre os candidatos está na obrigatoriedade de medidas de conservação ambiental no campo. Em um debate, Naig classificou Jones como uma voz isolada na defesa dessa exigência.

O setor agropecuário de Iowa resiste à adoção de regras obrigatórias. Entre os argumentos estão o fato de que nem todos os produtores são donos das terras onde trabalham e o risco de que algumas medidas reduzam os lucros, pelo menos no início.

Naig, que já trabalhou na fabricante de produtos químicos Monsanto, destacou os recordes alcançados pela secretaria durante o governo Reynolds. Segundo ele, as ações de conservação estão sendo ampliadas para que os resultados apareçam mais rápido.

“Esse tem sido um tema muito discutido na campanha”, disse Naig. Mas “precisamos olhar para essas questões no longo prazo, e estamos avançando”.

articles.title: 'Estoques no limite': guerra no Oriente Médio afeta abastecimento de diesel para agricultores no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Brasil importa 30% do combustível consumido. Apesar de relato dos produtores, ANP afirma que não existe risco de desabastecimento do produto no Rio Grande do Sul nem no restante do país.
articles.summary: Brasil importa 30% do combustível consumido. Apesar de relato dos produtores, ANP afirma que não existe risco de desabastecimento do produto no Rio Grande do Sul nem no restante do país.
articles.body:
Agricultores do Rio Grande do Sul estão preocupados com a escassez de óleo diesel às vésperas do plantio da safra de verão

A Sulpetro, entidade que representa os postos de combustíveis na região, diz que a redução dos estoques é reflexo dos conflitos no Oriente Médio, que pressionaram o preço do produto no mercado internacional. O Brasil importa 30% do diesel que consume.

"A importação está menor. Então, os estoques nacionais estão no limite do consumo. Não existe uma escassez, existe uma restrição. Não é falta de produto, é restrição e com preços elevados", afirma Fabrício Severo Braz, presidente da Sulpetro.

Segundo ele, muitos estados passaram a buscar o produto no Sul por causa do preço mais acessível.

O agricultor Arcênio Dupont está há 3 semanas com dificuldade para abastecer suas máquinas, no município de Santa Cruz do Sul. Ele diz que só conseguiu comprar mil litros do óleo diesel. Normalmente, ele consome 2 mil litros.

Em Julio de Castilhos a história se repete. A cooperativa que atende 6 mil produtores não tem recebido combustível suficiente dos distribuidores para atender toda a demanda.

O agricultor Sidnei Prates, de Santa Maria, precisou recorrer a postos de combustíveis para conseguir diesel para a colheita do arroz.

Mas até os postos enfrentam restrições. O empresário Antônio Palharin disse que recebeu apenas metade do diesel encomendado.

A Agencia Nacional do Petróleo ( ANP ) afirmou que não existe risco de desabastecimento de diesel no Rio Grande do Sul nem no restante do país.

Após os relatos dos agricultores gaúchos, a ANP informou que reforçou o monitoramento dos estoques e da distribuição do combustível.

articles.title: Global chip sell-off deepens as South Korean market plunges
articles.summary: Samsung and SK Hynix shares led the South Korean KOSPI lower as a global chip stock sell-off deepened.
articles.body:
A global sell-off in memory-chip stocks deepened overnight as South Korea's benchmark KOSPI ( ^KS11 ) tanked 7%.

Micron ( MU ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) were poised to open lower on Wednesday as SK Hynix ( 000660.KS ) and Samsung Electronics ( 005930.KS ) fell 10% and 8%, respectively, after tanking earlier this week over concerns about intensifying competition from China. The two memory giants account for more than half of the South Korean stock market's total capitalization.

The sell-off in South Korea followed a decline in the chip sector on Wall Street on Wednesday as worries about further rate hikes collided with fears of AI-driven debt financing.

Chip giant Nvidia ( NVDA ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), AMD ( AMD ), and Intel ( INTC ) all led the chip stocks lower during the session.

On Wednesday, worries about borrowing costs also hit the AI trade.

CoreWeave ( CRWV ) stock fell more than 15% after a chart of the neocloud providers' bond yields circulated on social media.

The stock's sharp sell-off highlighted concerns about the company's debt-heavy balance sheet and whether it can scale fast enough to manage its growing interest expense.

Any slowdown in AI spending could spell trouble for chip makers, which have been the main beneficiaries of infrastructure spending as hyperscalers race to build out data centers.

On Thursday, investors will get another glimpse of the health of the AI buildout when TSMC ( TSM ) reports quarterly results. Investors expect quarterly profits to rise 60%.

Investors will pay close attention to the foundry's capacity, given ASML's ( ASML ) results on Wednesday. The maker of advanced chip-making machines warned it may not be able to fully meet demand in 2027 and 2008.

Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: Iron Ore Trades Below $90 a Ton for First Time Since 2024
articles.summary: Iron ore futures in Singapore slipped to a two-year low under $90 a ton, extending a retreat fueled by soft demand in China and too much global supply.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Iron ore futures in Singapore slipped to a two-year low under $90 a ton, extending a retreat fueled by soft demand in China and too much global supply.

The steelmaking ingredient fell as much as 0.8% to $89.75 a ton, its weakest level on the Singapore Exchange since September 2024. Prices have slumped about 15% this year, with chronically weak construction activity in China keeping output under pressure at struggling steel plants.

"With steel mills still making very little money, there is still room for further cuts to hot metal production," Chaos Ternary Futures Co. wrote in a note. "Overall, we expect iron ore prices to remain range-bound with a downside bias in the short term."

China's crude steel output in the first eight months of this year was the lowest for the period since 2018 — a reflection of how the country's yearslong property slump has stifled demand. At the same time, supply of ore remains robust as new sources emerge, including Guinea's Simandou mine.

Futures in Singapore were 0.3% lower at $90.15 as of 11:10 a.m. local time. Iron ore also fell on the Dalian Commodity Exchange, while steel products retreated on the Shanghai Futures Exchange.

articles.title: The Jio IPO shareholder reservation explained: How RIL investors get a separate queue
articles.summary: As anticipation reaches a fever pitch for the blockbuster initial public offering (IPO) of Reliance Jio, a major detail has emerged that is bringing
articles.body: As anticipation reaches a fever pitch for the blockbuster initial public offering (IPO) of Reliance Jio, a major detail has emerged that is bringing significant cheer to the existing investor base of its parent company. Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) shareholders are getting their own dedicated category in the upcoming Jio IPO. According to the draft offer document, a specific portion of the shares will be reserved exclusively for existing individual RIL shareholders. This separate queue is designed to reward the loyal investor base while simultaneously ensuring massive retail participation in what is expected to be one of India’s largest-ever public market debuts.For those wondering how to get in on this exclusive reservation, the rules are strictly defined. According to financial portal IPO Market, citing the company's Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP), the shareholder reservation is open specifically to individual or Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) public shareholders of Reliance Industries.1 However, timing is everything. As per the draft filings, the eligibility of these shareholders will be determined on a fixed record date, which is set as the day the Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) is officially filed.1This strict timeline is highly significant because it effectively closes the window for opportunistic market players. Anyone hoping to quickly buy RIL shares on the eve of the IPO just to qualify for the Jio reservation will likely be left out if they miss this critical RHP filing date. Once the document is submitted to the market regulator, the list of eligible RIL shareholders is locked, securing the reservation strictly for those already holding the stock in their portfolios.Perhaps the most attractive feature of this reservation is the flexibility it offers to retail investors. Under the shareholder reservation, individual bids are capped at a maximum of ₹2 lakh.1 However, the real advantage lies in the ability to submit multiple applications across different categories. As noted by IPO Market, an eligible RIL investor can place a bid under the shareholder reservation portion and simultaneously place another bid in the general retail or non-institutional category.1Crucially, as per the established IPO rules cited by the portal, a reservation bid combined with a retail or non-institutional bid will not be treated or rejected as a "multiple bid".1 This unique structure essentially allows eligible RIL shareholders to take a "double dip," maximising their chances of securing an allotment in a public issue that is widely expected to be heavily oversubscribed.The draft document also lays out a clear roadmap for any shares that might remain unallocated. According to the company's proposed guidelines, in the unlikely event that the RIL shareholder reservation is not fully subscribed, those unsubscribed shares will first spill over into the employee reservation portion. If shares still remain untouched after that, they will be redirected to the general retail and non-institutional investor pools in a fixed 70:30 ratio. Furthermore, as highlighted by brokerage firm Ventura Securities, employees of the conglomerate are receiving their own separate reservation, and there is a combined category provision for individuals who happen to qualify for both, allowing them to maximize their participation.2Market experts point out that leveraging an existing base for a mega public issue has a highly successful precedent in the Indian equity markets. The closest parallel is the monumental Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) IPO in 2022. LIC introduced a 10% reservation specifically for its policyholders, backed by an aggressive PAN-linking campaign to ensure widespread participation.That strategy paid off handsomely. As reported by The Times of India at the time, the policyholder portion was a resounding success, eventually being subscribed over three times3. This dedicated reservation played a massive role in carrying the mammoth LIC issue over the finish line and famously brought millions of first-time retail investors into the stock market. By carving out a dedicated queue for RIL shareholders, Reliance Jio is deploying a similarly brilliant strategy to secure a guaranteed retail foundation for its stock market debut.References:IPO Market. articles.title: Smartphone Shipments Crash 22% in Worst Quarter Ever, IDC Says
articles.summary: The smartphone market suffered its worst decline on record in the September quarter, after rising memory costs pushed shipments down 22% with worse to come,...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The smartphone market suffered its worst decline on record in the September quarter, after rising memory costs pushed shipments down 22% with worse to come, according to market researcher IDC.

The higher cost of storage over the past year, led by demand from AI industry orders, has hurt profitability across the mobile sector and forced companies to raise prices, cut back specifications and discard budget-focused models, IDC said. Chinese brands like Xiaomi Corp. and Oppo took the worst hit among the top names, while Apple Inc. and Samsung Electronics Co. fared better due to their larger premium handset portfolios.

Device manufacturers are increasingly recognizing they're facing a permanent structural shift and IDC now expects any recovery in growth won't come until 2028, at the earliest. As companies increase prices and push consumers toward flagship or ultra models, the long-term trend is seen translating into greater share of a smaller market for Apple and other vendors with large-scale distribution and a premium mix of products.

"Current indicators suggest that the market has not yet reached the bottom," said IDC research director Nabila Popal. "Memory costs have surged approximately 350% since last year and are still rising, creating substantial pressure on vendor margins and shipments. The worst is yet to come."

articles.title: Copper Falls for Third Day as Strong US Inflation Spurs Selloff
articles.summary: Copper declined with other base metals after stronger-than-expected US consumer prices spurred bets on more aggressive tightening by the Federal Reserve.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Copper declined with other base metals after stronger-than-expected US consumer prices spurred bets on more aggressive tightening by the Federal Reserve.

A risk-off tone is sweeping markets — with technology stocks bearing the brunt — after data on Wednesday showed US inflation running at the fastest pace in five months. Copper on the London Metal Exchange was down 1.1% to $14,338 a ton by 12:11 p.m. Shanghai time, heading for a third daily decline.

The US inflation print raises the odds of more interest rate hikes by the Fed in coming months to cool the economy, an outcome that's potentially negative for metals by hurting demand and raising manufacturing costs. Copper reached a record high last month but has since wavered amid uncertainty over the Fed's pathway.

"The US CPI data was well beyond forecasts, strengthening inflation expectations and pressuring copper prices," Guangzhou Futures wrote in a note. Other metals also fell on the LME, with aluminum touching its lowest since last year.

Copper is still up more than 15% in 2026 after a huge flow of metal to the US — ahead of anticipated import tariffs — left markets elsewhere underserved. But optimism over demand from artificial intelligence infrastructure has also spurred copper bulls, making the metal exposed to headwinds for that sector.

AI stocks were among the biggest losers on Thursday as investors rushed from risk. South Korea's equity benchmark fell 8% as investors grow nervous about the sustainability of spending on the technology.

A decline for copper at market close would mark the metal's third daily drop — the longest such stretch since June.

articles.standfirst: Cada vez más inversores miran en el ladrillo para enriquecerse
articles.summary: Cada vez más inversores miran en el ladrillo para enriquecerse
articles.body: El rentismo es una de las tendencias más importantes en los últimos años de inversión en España entre la gente joven. Para que el dinero no se encuentre parado en el banco, son muchos los que optan por invertir en el ladrillo. En general, estas inversiones no son para la construcción de vivienda nueva, sino mediante la compra y adecuación de inmuebles para su posterior alquiler, sacando un rédito económico mensual. En este sentido, hay quienes compran y alquilan uno o dos pisos, pero también quienes fructifican en este ámbito y se convierten en grandes tenedores de vivienda en diferentes ciudades del país. Ciertamente, hay a quien le va tan bien que incluso puede jubilarse a una corta edad, como son los 33 años, y este es el caso de Carlos Galán. Este joven posee 20 pisos alquilados, pero lo más curioso es que él mismo vive también de alquiler, siendo esta una forma más de inversión de todas con las que cuenta al ahorrarse un buen dinero al mes: “Mis 20 pisos generan suficientes ingresos para cubrir mis gastos y más”, reconocía en un mensaje escrito por él mismo en la red social LinkedIn. Incluso, el joven ha reconocido poder jubilarse a tan pronta edad, aunque ha descartado dicha idea, ya que la inversión se ha convertido en una actividad que le gusta: “Para mí, la libertad financiera no es dejar de trabajar”. “Sería demasiado aburrido jubilarme a los 33 años, pero no sabría qué hacer con mi vida. Necesito un propósito y nuevos retos”, asegura el inversor quien reconoce que solo necesita dos horas al día para gestionar todos sus inmuebles, pues tiene gran parte del negocio delegado en terceras personas.

Además, se observa un bloque continuo de precios elevados desde las 18:00 hasta las 22:00, donde los valores superan constantemente los 230 €/MWh, siendo notablemente costosas las horas de 19:00 a 21:00. Esto revela un claro patrón en la demanda de energía durante estas franjas horarias. Las mejores oportunidades de ahorro en el precio de la luz se concentran durante las primeras horas del día y en la franja del mediodía. En particular, los tramos más destacados son de 12:00 a 15:00 donde los precios son especialmente bajos, alcanzando el valor más bajo de 68.24 €/MWh a las 13:00. articles.body: South Korea’s stock market hit a rough patch on Thursday, with the benchmark Kospi plunging 7.49% as technology stocks came under heavy selling pressure. The rout spread across Asian markets, prompting the country’s exchange operator to trigger a five-minute trading halt on programme sell orders after a sharp drop in index futures.The KOSPI dropped 450.02 points to 5,558.79, putting it on course for a seventh consecutive session of losses, its longest losing streak since September 2024. The index has fallen nearly 35% from its record high in June.The pressure on Asian equities followed a technology-led sell-off on Wall Street after US consumer price inflation accelerated more than expected in September. The data fuelled concerns that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates later this year, putting technology companies and AI-related stocks under further pressure.MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell 3.3%, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 4.8%. S&P 500 e-mini futures were down 0.5%.Samsung, SK Hynix lead South Korean market routMajor technology companies accounted for some of the steepest losses on the South Korean exchange. Samsung Electronics shares fell 9.05%, while SK Hynix dropped 11.06%, reflecting the broader weakness across Asia’s semiconductor supply chain.Battery maker LG Energy Solution lost 3.44%. Hyundai Motor declined 3.99%, while sister automaker Kia Corp fell 2.03%.The selling extended to other Asian technology companies. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) fell 2%, while Japan’s memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings plunged more than 11%. SoftBank Group, an investor in AI, declined 9.4%.Market breadth in South Korea remained heavily negative. Of the 889 stocks traded, 768 declined and 90 advanced. Foreign investors sold shares worth a net 355.6 billion won.The won, meanwhile, strengthened 0.21% to 1,339.5 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform, compared with its previous close of 1,342.3.‘Sidecar’ triggeredThe sharp decline prompted the South Korean exchange operator to activate a sell-side “sidecar”, an automatic mechanism designed to temporarily cool trading during periods of heavy selling. articles.title: G20 finance ministers, central bankers gather amid fallout from Iran war
articles.summary: Officials meet in Thailand as conflict drives energy prices higher and casts uncertainty over global economy.
articles.body:
The G20 finance ministers and central bank governors are gathering in Bangkok, Thailand, on Thursday amid an uncertain global outlook shaped by the US-Israel war on Iran.

The meetings are being held in conjunction with the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank, taking place in the Thai capital from October 12 to October 18.

Here are some of the key details about the meetings:

What are the G20, the IMF and the World Bank?

The G20 is an economic forum comprising 19 large economies, including the United States, China, the United Kingdom, Australia, Brazil, India, Japan, Indonesia and Saudi Arabia, as well as the European Union and the African Union.

The grouping has an annually rotating presidency, currently held by the US.

Together, the G20 countries account for about 85 percent of global gross domestic product (GDP) and three-quarters of global trade.

The G20 was established in 1999 as a forum for finance ministers and central bank governors to address shared economic concerns in the wake of the Asian Financial Crisis, before expanding into a broader forum for national leaders.

The IMF, based in Washington, DC, is an international financial institution that promotes international cooperation on monetary policy, trade and economic growth.

Its membership includes all but a handful of the world’s sovereign states, including North Korea, Cuba, the Vatican City and Monaco.

The World Bank, also based in Washington, DC, primarily serves as a provider of loans and grants to developing countries. It has 189 member countries.

The IMF and the World Bank were created at the 1944 Bretton Woods conference in the US, convened by the Allied Powers to establish the contours of the post-World War II international financial order.

Most finance ministers and central bank governors of the G20 will be in Bangkok, along with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva and World Bank Group President Ajay Banga.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will be a notable absence from the gatherings, as the top economic official of the world’s biggest economy and G20 chair.

US officials have cited “domestic engagements” for Bessent’s decision to skip the events, at which Washington will be represented by Deputy Secretary Francis Brooke and Undersecretary for International Affairs Erin Browne.

The G20 meeting, one of several gatherings of the group’s finance ministers each year, will help shape the agenda for the headline leaders’ summit in Miami, Florida, taking place on December 14-15.

The economic fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran is expected to dominate discussions.

Attacks across the Middle East have upended economic activity across the region, while disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz has driven a surge in energy prices worldwide.

Crude oil prices have exceeded $100 a barrel for much of the past eight months, placing a strain on government coffers and household budgets, particularly in the Gulf region and the rest of Asia.

In advance of the meeting, Australia’s Treasurer Jim Chalmers MP said he would use the discussions to call for an end to the conflicts in the Middle East and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz “because that’s what the global economy desperately needs”.

“The war in the Middle East is having a devastating economic impact and is pushing up fuel prices, inflation and interest rates around the world,” Chalmers said in a statement.

Other issues likely to feature on the agenda include the ballooning debt levels of many countries, which exceed 100 percent of GDP in the US, Canada, Japan, Italy and France.

In a speech on Wednesday, Georgieva warned that mounting debt posed a threat to the global economy and that there was no “magic” formula that would allow governments to avoid tax hikes or spending cuts.

G20 members will also bring more specific individual concerns to the table based on their economic and geopolitical priorities.

The US, for example, has repeatedly expressed concern about “global imbalances”, a veiled reference to China’s state-driven industrial model that has allowed Chinese exporters to flood overseas markets with cheap goods.

US President Donald Trump has long claimed that China’s large trade surplus, which stood at a cumulative $938bn in September, proves that international trade is stacked against US manufacturers.

In a statement addressed to the IMF on Wednesday, Bessent called for action to address mismatched trade balances.

“This especially includes strengthening its analysis and engagement on the role non-market policies and practices and exchange rates play in driving external imbalances,” Bessent said.

“Policymakers around the world are having difficult discussions about how to sustain market-based systems amid distortionary policies from some economies that skew competition and hurt employment.”

Divisions and competing interests cloud the prospects for coordination, however.

At the last meeting of G20 finance ministers in Asheville, North Carolina, US, held on August 31 and September 1, member countries failed to issue a joint communique after China objected to language to do with trade.

articles.title: 12,700 US-based tech professionals returned to India in 9 months; 2026 may beat last year's record as H-1B visa uncertainty grows, but returnees face steep salary cuts at home
articles.summary: Thousands of US-based Indian techies are returning to India to a job market that does not offer similar salary levels.
articles.body: Thousands of US-based Indian techies are returning to India to a job market that does not offer similar salary levels. But, the number of such returnees is increasing as visa uncertainties weigh under the Donald Trump administration.As the number of technology professionals returning from the US continues to rise, India could be heading towards a reversal in the movement of talent between the two countries.Between January and September 2026, around 12,700 white-collar technology workers returned to India, according to data sourced from staffing firm Xpheno by ET. The tally is already approaching the record 15,100 returnees recorded in the whole of 2025, and is expected to surpass that figure by the end of this year.Indian techies return from the USThe increase has been consistent over the past few years. Xpheno's data puts the number of professionals who moved back to India at 7,200 in 2023, rising to 9,800 in 2024 before reaching last year's peak. The figures cover white-collar technology workers moving in either direction between India and the US, rather than only those travelling on H-1B visas.The growing flow of returnees could eventually leave India with a net gain in technology talent from the US, meaning more professionals would be moving back home than heading there.For now, however, the outbound movement remains higher. Nearly 14,500 people moved from India to the US up to September this year, Xpheno's figures show.Kamal Karanth, cofounder of Xpheno, told the financial daily that the number of technology professionals returning to India this year was on track to exceed the 2025 total, further narrowing the difference between inbound and outbound talent flows.He also indicated that the recent H-1B move could accelerate the shift, potentially pushing the number of returnees above the count of technology professionals leaving India for the US.The changing pattern of migration is partly linked to uncertainty over US immigration rules and economic policies, along with the tightening of visa regulations over the past few years, experts said. Rising layoffs at large technology companies in the US during the last two to three years could also be contributing to the trend.Xpheno's assessment draws on several sources, including its internal database of candidates, its recruitment management system and job boards used for hiring in India and overseas. The staffing firm examines these records from a recruiter's standpoint to identify patterns in cross-border talent movement, professional experience and compensation.Job issuesReturning to India with years of professional experience does not necessarily make finding a suitable job any easier. The current hiring environment has been particularly difficult for technology professionals coming back from the US, said Kamal Karanth, cofounder of staffing firm Xpheno.“Considering the dynamics and trends of active demand in the Indian job market, it has not been the best of times for US returnees,” Karanth said.He pointed out that the Indian technology sector has struggled to maintain consistent hiring momentum since the surge in recruitment in 2021. “After the hiring buoyancy of 2021, the Indian tech sector’s talent action has not had a period of stability extending beyond a quarter,” he noted.Neeti Sharma, chief executive of staffing firm TeamLease Digital, said companies in India are taking a more selective approach to recruitment. Rather than treating overseas experience as a major advantage, employers are placing greater emphasis on candidates' specialised skills and relevant work experience.According to Sharma, the strongest demand is for professionals with expertise in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, data and product leadership. Skills in cloud computing, cybersecurity and implementing AI solutions across enterprises are also sought after.Pay is another significant hurdle for professionals returning from the US. Depending on their role, employer, location and project experience, many may have to settle for salaries equivalent to just 25% to 33% of what they earned overseas, experts said.Xpheno's data puts the average annual salary of a full-stack engineer working in the US on an H-1B visa at $105,000, with earnings typically ranging from $70,000 to $150,000. In India, however, professionals with comparable skills and experience who rank among the top 1% can earn between $20,000 and $32,000 annually.Indian employers are largely maintaining compensation levels in line with domestic salary structures instead of matching pay packages offered in overseas markets. As a result, professionals returning from the US may need to lower their salary expectations to secure suitable positions.Sharma said applied AI professionals in India can earn annual salaries of around Rs 16 lakh to Rs 35 lakh, equivalent to approximately $16,800 to $36,800. Senior specialists, however, can command significantly higher compensation.Global capability centres (GCCs) in India are another potential source of employment for returning professionals. However, those seeking jobs at these centres must compete with experienced candidates who are already available in the domestic talent pool.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: El experto financiero no ve la ventaja del partido socialista con la normativa que quiere implantar
articles.body: El 29 de noviembre se acerca y los partidos ya han empezado a decidir cuál va a ser el asunto central de su campaña. Después de que el adelanto electoral fuese provocado por la negativa del Congreso a los decretos de vivienda, el PSOE ha centrado su discurso en erigirse como la única fuerza capaz de dar soluciones a este problema. Así pues, los decretos de vivienda han continuado hacia adelante. Ambos textos están pendientes de su votación y convalidación por parte de la Diputación Permanente del Congreso. Para Pedro Sánchez no es suficiente: “Hemos tomado medidas que benefician al inquilino y al pequeño propietario. Pero el problema está arriba, en los aticazos y en los fondos buitre. Vamos a acabar con la especulación y con los abusos”. A pesar de que la campaña del PSOE gira en torno a la vivienda, Gonzalo Bernardos no cree que sus medidas le vayan a favorecer de cara a las elecciones. De hecho, considera que el partido que más ventaja va a obtener de este asunto no es el socialista, sino Sumar. Así lo ha explicado en un post en sus redes sociales. “Ha de estar muy desorientado el PSOE para pensar que medidas que van contra los propietarios de viviendas le van a proporcionar votos. A Sumar puede ser que sí, pero al PSOE le van a restar sufragios. No obstante, el tiempo lo dirá”, analiza el experto financiero en su cuenta de X. Por ahora, este miércoles, 14 de octubre, salió el barómetro del CIS y los resultados son positivos para la formación liderada por Sánchez. Sitúa al PSOE como primera formación en intención de voto, con el 34 por ciento, 12 puntos por encima del Partido Popular. Mientras tanto, deja a VOX como tercera fuerza y a Sumar/Frente Amplio como la cuarta.

articles.title: Figma sees design as key differentiator as AI  lowers coding barriers: CEO Dylan Field
articles.summary: Figma CEO Dylan Field says as AI lowers coding barriers, design becomes the key differentiator. Figma expands in India, adds AI tools like Code Layers and Specs.
articles.body: As AI makes coding faster and lowers the barriers to building software, the value in technology development will increasingly shift towards design, where understanding users, business needs and cultural context will remain critical, Figma CEO and cofounder Dylan Field said.Field, who is visiting India for the first time, said the country’s pragmatic approach to technology adoption stood out compared with San Francisco, where experimentation often generates considerable noise. Indian companies were focused on identifying what would advance their businesses and deliver tangible returns, he said.“Some people here might already be ahead of people in San Francisco. There is a lot of noise there, with people trying a lot of things. Some of those things are great. They will be the future. But there is also a lot of noise that does not work out,” Field said.AI’s ability to perform tasks with verifiable outcomes, such as mathematics, cybersecurity and coding, is advancing rapidly. But designing systems that are maintainable, extensible and aligned with business needs remains more complex, he said. Design involves multiple possible solutions, requiring an understanding of users, culture, business problems and aesthetics.“Design is this combinatorial explosion of options where there is no one right answer,” Field said. “You are trying to connect to the culture, business problems and users. You need to have great empathy. These are not things AI is amazing at.” In 2022, Adobe announced plans to acquire Figma in a $20 billion cash-and-stock deal. However, the proposed acquisition collapsed in December 2023 amid regulatory hurdles.AI-generated content can also struggle to stand out because it often resembles existing work, potentially undermining trust, he said. Products that attract users are those that demonstrate craft, care and intention. Rather than replacing human creativity, AI can provide an initial output that designers refine to reflect their own thinking.Field said this shift would not make engineers redundant. Figma continues to hire engineers who can think through systems rather than merely use AI tools. As AI gets better at translating designs into code, the development process can focus more on exploring alternatives and deciding what to build, rather than only how to build it.Figma is developing tools that allow users to move between design and code on the same canvas, bringing in context from coding agents and specifications. Its Model Context Protocol (MCP) also allows users to take design context into external tools to accelerate development.The company is expanding its India operations, which began about a year ago with go-to-market, sales and customer-support functions. It is now adding designer and developer advocates, with product and engineering potentially following as the team grows.India is a priority market for Figma, with its second-largest daily active user base, Field said. However, supporting customers remains the immediate focus.Figma is also seeking to improve the efficiency of AI-assisted development. Its Code Connect tool maps design systems to components and tokens in code, reducing the need for AI models to search for matching elements. Field said this saves customers 25-33% in token costs.Figma unveiled AI-powered features at Config India in Bengaluru to help design, product and engineering teams collaborate on a shared canvas, build code-backed prototypes and develop websites using real data.The updates include Code Layers for creating and editing prototypes on the design canvas, Figma Specs for aligning teams on product requirements and guiding AI agents, and Payload for building data-backed websites and internal tools.“Customers often tell us they prefer working together with their teams on the canvas rather than alone with coding agents in a terminal or IDE,” Field said. Code Layers is launching in open beta.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Big items are done': Sergio Gor gives update on India-US trade deal, Trump's 100% sanctions threat
articles.summary: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor on Thursday said the two countries had wrapped up the major items on their trade deal agenda, with negotiations moving
articles.body: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor on Thursday said the two countries had wrapped up the major items on their trade deal agenda, with negotiations moving at an “incredible pace”. Drawing a comparison with the India-EU trade pact, Gor highlighted the speed of the US talks, saying a deal was announced within weeks of his arrival in India, while negotiations for the European Union agreement took nearly two decades.Commenting on America’s 100% tariff for Russian gas and oil buyers, he said that US President Donald Trump is expected to take a decision within the next 10 days. Gor said that the legislation, which received 86 votes in the 100-member US Senate, gives the President the authority to impose sanctions on countries involved in buying Russian oil and gas or helping others evade sanctions. However, he maintained that the measures were not designed to target India or any other individual country.“...We have ongoing discussions on that as it passed with overwhelming bipartisan support. That law got 86 votes out of 100 in our Senate... These sanctions options that Congress passed, they are not targeted at any individual country. It is three different buckets; one is oil, the second is gas, the third is sanctions evasion.”He further added that these nations are identified based on numbers.“It just happens that India does fall in one of those buckets, along with a lot of other countries. The goal is not to punish anyone. The goal is to try to bring an end to this war. I do think the president will make a determination on that over the next few days...”The law requires Trump to make a determination within 30 days of its passage. Gor said that no country had yet been sanctioned under the legislation and that any decision on exemptions or relief for India would be up to the President.“He has to make a determination in the next I believe 10 or so days,” Gor said.ALSO READ: Many Indians willingly joining Russian forces, government informs SCIndia-US trade deal: ‘ big items are done’Alongside the discussions on sanctions, Gor expressed confidence that India and the US would soon reach a trade agreement, saying the negotiations had advanced considerably despite the challenges involved.“The big picture, the big framework, the big items are done,” he said, describing the outstanding matters as smaller details and issues that could arise as talks continued.The negotiations have now been under way for around a year and a half.Gor said that the pace of discussions compared favourably with other trade agreements, while noting that the US had to revisit parts of an earlier arrangement after the Supreme Court ruled the law underpinning it unconstitutional.He pointed to the speed of engagement since his arrival in India as a reason for optimism, contrasting the process with the time taken to negotiate the European Union trade deal.“...Within three weeks of arriving here, we announced a trade deal... The European Union trade deal took almost 20 years. So we're at an incredible pace, and I am confident that we will get it done.”US firms and their Indian presenceGor said that American businesses had significant opportunities in India, thanks to the country's market and government's approach to overseas investment. He highlighted defence manufacturing, IT, data centres and chip manufacturing as areas where companies from the two countries were already working together.“...You have an unmatched market here for our companies... For the private sector to be able to come to India to compete, to have their foot in the door, you have a very pragmatic prime minister here that welcomes outside investment. Pick any sector, and we're working together at it.”Naming the sectors where India excels, the US ambassador said, “If you look at the defence world, we have co-production happening here in India. If you look at IT, it's unmatched. Google, Microsoft, Adobe, Micron; every one of them is opening data centres and chip manufacturing here that work with our companies hand in hand in the United States. So when a job is created in India, a counter job is created in the United States. It is an incredible win-win situation that I would say is unmatched. We're actively engaged...”According to Gor, investment in India can generate employment opportunities on both sides, with US companies working alongside their American counterparts even as they expand operations in India. He added that the two countries were actively engaged across sectors and reiterated his confidence in the trade negotiations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body:
LONDON/HONG KONG, Oct 15 (Reuters) - The dollar slipped from an 18-month peak on Thursday in choppy trading as a sharp drop in Treasury yields weighed on the greenback, while cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials ‌tempered October hike expectations despite hot inflation data.

The dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of ‌peers, was last down 0.2% on the day at 102.03, having hit an 18-month high on Wednesday after US inflation figures came in stronger than expected.

That helped the euro ​bounce 0.5% from an 18-month trough to $1.1216, putting it on track for its biggest daily gain in nearly two months. Sterling strengthened 0.5% to $1.3253, remaining broadly steady after data showed that Britain's economy unexpectedly grew 0.1% in August.

Markets turned risk-off as the hot US CPI reading bolstered bets on higher-for-longer Fed rates and revived worries about AI companies' heavy debt burdens, driving safe-haven flows into Treasuries.

The rally in US government bonds pushed the ‌benchmark 10-year yield to 5.0892% while the 30-year yield ⁠dipped to 5.4319%, both touching around three-week lows.

As well as the moves in bond yields and jittery equities, with tech stocks especially taking a hit, Kit Juckes, chief FX strategist at Societe Generale, also noted ⁠that shifts in positioning played a role in the dollar's moves.

"The overall picture is I think one of a little bit of a tug of war between people who would like to look for a correction in the dollar. Because positioning's too big, we've come a long way, there's not really ​much ​new news, we've got a lot of rate hikes priced in and ​so on. And then the economic data, which can ‌flip it," he said.

"I suspect it'll be choppy and uncomfortable until we've got past the retail sales and PPI numbers."

Both data points are due later in the day, with producer prices expected to show a jump in business costs last month.

Market pricing for an October Fed rate hike rose sharply to 50% on the back of the CPI data, before a chorus of Fed officials – including Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly – said the central bank could wait for a clearer picture ahead of the ‌October 27 and 28 meeting, tempering those bets.

"Despite the whole CPI number coming ​slightly stronger than expected, I think markets have sort of taken the view ​that maybe it was not hot enough to force the ​Fed's hand for October," said Khoon Goh, the head of Asia research at ANZ.

articles.title: Iraq devalues dinar to ease cash crunch, leaving traders in limbo
articles.summary: The government hopes a weaker dinar will help pay salaries, but traders face rising import costs and uncertainty.
articles.body:
Baghdad, Iraq – Sitting anxiously in his small office in Jameela market, one of Baghdad’s main wholesale markets, food trader Hamza al-Rudayni is waiting to see what the coming days will bring.

A decision by the Iraqi government to devalue the country’s currency, the dinar, against the US dollar has left traders like him facing sudden losses and uncertainty over the prices they should charge for their goods.

“I don’t know what to do,” al-Rudayni told Al Jazeera after the devaluation reduced the dollar value of his dinar holdings, leaving him with less money to purchase imported goods.

“All I know is I woke up a few days ago to discover that I had lost 25 million Iraqi dinars (roughly $16,500 at the new exchange rate) because of this decision, while larger merchants lost billions,” he said.

Al-Rudayni entered the wholesale trade market last year after losing his previous job at a private Iraqi bank that he says was sanctioned by the United States Treasury. He sold his car and used his savings to start trading with a larger merchant before recently launching his own business.

With exchange-rate fluctuations making prices unpredictable, al-Rudayni said he and many other traders have chosen to suspend buying and selling until the situation stabilises.

“Market activity has ground to a halt,” al-Rudayni said. “Traders buy goods in dollars but sell them in dinars, as regulations prohibit them from selling in dollars.”

That is the root of the problem for traders: A weaker dinar means they have to pay more in local currency for goods imported in dollars, while making it harder to determine the right price they should charge customers for goods they already have in stock.

On October 7, the Iraqi government introduced a new official exchange rate against the US dollar, in an attempt to ease a financial crisis triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran and the disruption of oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz.

Before the war, Iraq exported around 3.5 million barrels of oil per day through the Strait of Hormuz, accounting for 90 percent of Iraq’s government revenue.

The Central Bank of Iraq decision set the rate at 1,520 dinars per US dollar for cash sales to the public. It was previously set at 1,320 dinars per dollar.

Devaluing the Iraqi dinar by almost 15 percent against the dollar allows the government to receive more local currency for every dollar of oil revenue it converts, helping it cover public spending, including government employee salaries.

“It is my decision and I am responsible for it,” Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said during a meeting with parliamentary leaders on Thursday.

“I was facing three challenging options to cover salaries and other mandatory expenditures,” al-Zaidi added. “The first is to cut salaries by 35 percent … the second is to pay the salaries every 45 days … while the third is to resort to foreign loans.”

Al-Zaidi, a former banker, also said that his government had inherited public debt exceeding 208 trillion Iraqi dinars ($139bn at the new rate) when it took office in May. He said the government needed approximately 10 trillion dinars ($6.7bn) each month to cover salaries and other essential expenditure.

The crisis in the Strait of Hormuz had caused a severe financial squeeze for the Iraqi government.

Although the situation has eased somewhat in recent weeks after Iraq’s oil exports partially recovered, they have yet to return to their pre-war levels.

Mudher Mohammed Salih, the Iraqi prime minister’s financial adviser, said in August that the Central Bank of Iraq’s foreign currency reserves had declined from $106bn to approximately $80bn.

To make up for the loss of revenue, the Iraqi government has also turned to borrowing from domestic banks to cover salaries and other expenses.

A Finance Ministry official told Al Jazeera that ensuring salaries were paid on time remained the government’s main priority, describing this issue as a matter of domestic economic stability.

“Our hands are tied regarding the revenue and how to maintain enough money to ensure that we can pay the salaries,” the official, who asked to remain anonymous because he was not authorised to speak publicly, said.

Economists have warned that while adjusting the exchange rate could ease some immediate fiscal pressures, it would not address the deeper weaknesses in Iraq’s economy.

“Nothing in economics is sacred, including the exchange rate,” said Nabil al-Marsoumi, professor of economics at Al Maaqal University in Basra. “It can be adjusted, but only after all other options have been exhausted.”

“In any case, the exchange rate shouldn’t be used as a cover-up for failures in the state’s economic and fiscal policies,” he added.
