articles.title: Indian higher education in 2030: The changes shaping its future
articles.summary: By 2030, the university experience in India will look substantially different; not only in what students study, but also in how they learn and prepare for
articles.body: By 2030, the university experience in India will look substantially different; not only in what students study, but also in how they learn and prepare for their careers. The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 has provided a framework for this transformation, while technology and changing expectations from students and employers are accelerating the transition. Institutions that adapt early will shape the learning experience for the next generation.1. Flexibility becomes the defaultThe rigid, single-stream degree is evolving towards multidisciplinary learning. Students are increasingly able to combine majors and minors, cross over between fields, and build a programme around their interests rather than fit into a fixed template. The Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) supports this by letting learners earn, store and transfer credits across institutions, with multiple entry and exit points along the way. The system is already being implemented: as of mid-2026, nearly 2,900 higher education institutions had registered on the government's ABC portal, and more than 26 crore APAAR IDs, linked to it under the “one nation, one student ID” initiative, had been issued across school and higher education.By 2030, an engineering student minoring in design, or a commerce student studying psychology, should be a normal part of campus life.2. AI Moves from novelty to infrastructureArtificial intelligence will be part of how universities teach, assess and operate. The shift is already underway at scale: the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) declared 2025 the “Year of AI,” promoting AI integration into core engineering curricula across disciplines, across more than 14,000 approved colleges and roughly 40 million students.The greater challenge is pedagogical. If AI can produce a competent first draft in seconds, universities must rethink what they assess: critical thinking, original argument, ethical judgement and the ability to question a machine's output. AI literacy will become a core competency, taught across disciplines.3. Skills matter as much as degreesEmployers increasingly assess what a graduate can do, not only what they studied. Universities are responding with internships, industry projects, live case studies and hands-on labs built into the curriculum. NEP 2020 guidelines encourage internships within undergraduate programs to provide practical exposure. Working on real-world problems also helps students develop problem-solving abilities and teamwork. By 2030, experiential learning will be an integral part of higher education. Institutions will be recognized for their ability to prepare graduates for employment.4. Internationaliszation comes homeIndian students have long looked abroad for a global education, but that landscape is changing. Under the UGC’s 2023 regulations, foreign universities can now set up degree-granting campuses in India, and the first of them have already opened their doors. A parallel track has emerged at GIFT City in Gujarat, where international universities have established campuses under a separate regulatory framework, offering programmes in areas such as finance, business and STEM.The result is a wider set of options at home. Students can gain global exposure through exchange semesters, joint programmes and, increasingly, full foreign degrees, without having to leave India for their entire education.5. Innovation and entrepreneurship move to the centreIndia's startup ecosystem is one of the largest in the world, and universities are becoming its early launchpads. Incubators, maker spaces, pre-incubation programs and prototyping labs are turning campuses into places where ideas become products. A student with an idea in second year should be able to find mentorship, space and connections to seed funding on campus.Universities that treat innovation as a core function, supported within the curriculum, will help nurture more job creators, not only job seekers.6. Research becomes centralIndia's ambition to become a knowledge economy depends on stronger research. Expect more interdisciplinary research centrescenters, more industry-sponsored projects, greater emphasis on intellectual property, and earlier exposure to research for undergraduates. The aim is a culture where research becomes part of the learning experience right from the first year.Domain-specific research in agriculture, healthcare, space technology, energy and climate will create opportunities to address challenges such as sustainable farming, accessible diagnostics, satellite communication, clean energy and climate resilience. These areas will require collaboration across disciplines and offer students opportunities to work on problems with practical and societal relevance.7. Wellbeing and inclusion become institutional prioritiesStudent mental health, financial access and inclusion are becoming central institutional concerns.. Counselling services, scholarships, financial aid and support for first-generation learners will increasingly be seen as basic parts of a quality institution, integral to student support.What this means for universitiesThe next decade will require institutions to combine academic rigor with adaptability. This requires offering flexible, multidisciplinary pathways, embedding technology thoughtfully, connecting learning to the real world, fostering research and innovation, strengthening global collaboration, and supporting students’ holistic development.Somaiya Vidyavihar University, with its wide range of schools and programmes across disciplines, its emphasis on experiential learning, and its international collaborations, reflects many of these shifts. These priorities shape a student-centric learning environment that combines academic depth with practical relevance. The direction is clear: education that is flexible, global, practical and human.The universities that thrive in 2030 will be the ones that prepare thoughtfully today and act consistently in the years ahead.By Dr Suresh K. articles.title: Trump administration doubles its equity stake in GlobalFoundries, will partner with company in new semiconductor plant
articles.summary: President Trump and chipmaker GlobalFoundries announced a deal Wednesday, doubling what was already a sizable US government stake in the company.
articles.body:
President Trump and chipmaker GlobalFoundries ( GFS ) announced a multifaceted series of deals Wednesday, doubling what was already a sizable US government stake in the company, as well as plans for two new semiconductor fabrication plants to be operated by the company and the US and Japanese governments.

GlobalFoundries' market capitalization, according to Yahoo Finance data , is about $27.2 billion. Trump said Wednesday the US government's stake is now "worth over 2 Billion Dollars."

The deal also includes the formation of a new "Special Purpose Vehicle" co-owned by the US and Japanese governments. The new entity will fund construction of the two fabrication plants and then own the underlying infrastructure, according to a presentation from GlobalFoundries to its investors.

GlobalFoundries will receive payments for its technological know-how and for operating the facility, with the company describing itself as the "the technology provider and operator" of the plants.

The announcements on Wednesday were the latest twist in the US government's aggressive move into equity stakes in private companies, which now spans 35 companies.

The overlapping GlobalFoundries deals also include reallocating a previous $955 million US government award made under the 2022 Chips and Science Act toward modernizing the company's facilities.

Trump, in his social media post , directly linked the $955 million to an increased equity stake, saying that money "brings our total Investments to 1.63 Billion Dollars, and now, the U.S. Government's stake is worth over 2 Billion Dollars."

GlobalFoundries described the two as separate agreements but confirmed that the US government is taking an additional stake of approximately 4% of the company.

The company hasn't released full details of the previous deals, but a company official confirmed to Yahoo Finance that those prior equity stakes totaled between 3% and 4%, resulting in a current government stake approaching 8%.

The math in Trump's post about a more than $2 billion stake in a $27.2 billion company implies an equity stake of at least 7.35%.

A continued role for the US and Japanese governments

GlobalFoundries also announced plans to help build two semiconductor fabrication plants, which Trump described as a $21 billion investment paid for by Japan.

Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry confirmed some of the details of the deal in a press release Thursday and added that the plant would provide Japanese companies with increased business opportunities including in supplying manufacturing equipment.

articles.title: SpaceX’s Spectrum Purchase Exposes Risks for Big Telecom Stocks
articles.summary: Telecom stocks have long been considered a relatively safe bet for investors, offering predictable growth, limited downside and healthy dividends. But a comb...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Telecom stocks have long been considered a relatively safe bet for investors, offering predictable growth, limited downside and healthy dividends. But a combination of competition from SpaceX and rising Treasury yields is threatening to upend that equation.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp. announced last week that it's buying a swath of spectrum that will enable it to beam cellular service from its Starlink satellites, potentially setting up Elon Musk's aerospace technology company to become a major mobile carrier as well. Verizon Communications Inc., AT&T Inc., and T-Mobile US Inc. all suffered double-digit percentage declines on Friday after the news hit.

"Competitive risk is presenting itself in a way it hasn't in the past," said John Conca, a telecom analyst at Third Bridge Group. "The market perception is that this is just the first shoe dropping."

The telecommunications players were already under pressure from soaring interest rates. The yield on 10-year Treasuries crossed 5% on Sept. 15, and since then shares of Verizon and AT&T are down 14% while T-Mobile's have lost 13%. The companies are sensitive to bond yields because part of their appeal is based on their reliable dividend payouts.

"Some people buy them for their (dividend) yields on the idea that it comes with a growth kicker," said Michael Cuggino, president and portfolio manager at Permanent Portfolio Family of Funds. "But they're not growing very much, and there are risks to that growth down the road with this SpaceX question. At the same time, the yields don't look nearly as attractive as they might otherwise, because you can get a similar yield from risk-free Treasuries."

T-Mobile shares are down 22% this year, while AT&T has lost 7.2%. Verizon is up 9.1% but still trails the S&P 500 Index's 13% gain. SpaceX went public in June and the stock has jumped 13% from its IPO price, though it's 25% below the peak it hit within days of the IPO.

Of course, the threat from SpaceX is pretty far down the road considering it will need a lot of costly terrestrial infrastructure to effectively compete, especially in densely-populated markets, according to Conca. However, this is compounding pre-existing concerns about the pace of growth in the industry.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday virtually inaugurated five development projects worth around Rs 3,350 crore in Ladakh, covering airport infrastructure, strategic road connectivity, renewable energy and water conservation.“Today, another chapter is being added to Ladakh’s progress and development. I am happy to be part of this occasion through technology. Several important development projects have been inaugurated in Ladakh today,” PM Modi said while inaugurating the projects, PTI reported.“These projects will make travel easier for many people, improve electricity facilities in some areas, increase water availability in others, and strengthen the preservation of our ancient heritage,” he added.The five key projects include:A new passenger terminal at Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport in LehThe 298-km Nimmu-Padum-Darcha RoadThe 9 MW Hanu Hydroelectric Project and power transmission infrastructureIndia’s first Petroglyph Conservation Park in Leh40 water bodies across 40 villages under Project Amrit Him SarovarNew Leh airport terminalThe new passenger terminal at Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport in Leh has been built at a cost of Rs 640 crore. Spread over 23,800 square metres, it is designed to handle 35 lakh passengers annually, officials said.The terminal incorporates geothermal energy to improve energy efficiency and reduce its carbon footprint, an important consideration in Ladakh’s ecologically sensitive environment.Combining modern passenger amenities with elements of Ladakh’s cultural heritage, the terminal is expected to improve passenger convenience and strengthen air connectivity with the rest of the country.PM inaugurated several other projectsPM Modi also dedicated to the nation the 298-km Nimmu-Padum-Darcha Road, constructed by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO).The road connects Nimmu in Leh with Darcha in Himachal Pradesh through the remote Zanskar Valley. It provides an alternative route to Ladakh, supplementing the Srinagar-Leh and Manali-Leh highways, an official statement said.The road crosses challenging Himalayan terrain, including the high-altitude Shinkun La Pass. Its strategic importance lies in improving the movement of personnel and supplies for the armed forces, the statement said.It is also expected to benefit residents of Zanskar by improving access to healthcare, education, markets and other essential services.As part of efforts to strengthen energy security and tap Ladakh’s renewable energy potential, the prime minister inaugurated the 9 MW Hanu small hydroelectric project and the 66 kV double-circuit Dah-Hanu-Khaltsi transmission line.The projects are expected to strengthen power evacuation infrastructure and improve the reliability of the region’s electricity network, supporting the use of Ladakh’s hydropower resources.The Prime Minister also inaugurated India’s first Petroglyph Conservation Park at Sindhu Ghat in Leh to protect Ladakh’s archaeological heritage.The region is home to hundreds of prehistoric rock art sites featuring carvings of wildlife, human figures and symbolic representations. These carvings offer insights into thousands of years of human history.The conservation park is aimed at preserving this heritage for future generations.The prime minister also inaugurated 40 water bodies developed across 40 villages under Project Him Sarovar. The initiative seeks to address Ladakh’s geographical and climatic challenges through water conservation and aligns with the objectives of Mission Amrit Sarovar.Agriculture in Ladakh faces a seasonal mismatch between water availability and demand. Farmers often experience shortages during the crucial sowing season, even though snowmelt and glacial runoff provide substantial water resources at other times of the year.Project Him Sarovar aims to conserve water when it is available and make it accessible when needed. The initiative is expected to support irrigation, sustain agricultural livelihoods and strengthen long-term water security in the region, the official statement said.You use AI every day. articles.title: CoreWeave is getting drilled again the day after a panic-filled rout
articles.summary: CRWV on the rocks.
articles.body:
Heavily indebted AI player CoreWeave ( CRWV ) is having an awful week that keeps getting worse.

Shares plunged 6% in pre-market trading on Thursday following a 15% rout on Wednesday.

"In our view, the company's long-term business model remains economically challenged; we maintain our Underperform," Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei said in a note Thursday.

Two factors collided to spark Wednesday's sell-off.

One, CoreWeave's corporate bonds across maturities continued to be dumped on fears of an AI slowdown and what that would mean for the company's precarious balance sheet.

The rise in yields on CoreWeave's bonds even spurred Elon Musk to post "Yikes" on X in response to a post by venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya.

Two, Gartner, in a new report, forecast that by 2030 "cost pressure and a lack of a differentiating business model will force over 80% of neocloud providers to cease independent operations."

CoreWeave is a neocloud. The report essentially was akin to yelling fire in a crowded theater.

CoreWeave sought to push back on the bears, but it doesn't appear to have worked.

"Net net, this market is dynamic, and there are many players. But not all companies are following the same playbook we are. Others are trying to raise enormous amounts of capital without the execution, revenue, scale, or software solutions that CoreWeave delivers to its customers. When you are building a new type of technology company there will be periods of time when the market misunderstands and acts irrationally. We are confident in our business model, our customers, the extraordinary quality of our execution, and the relentless discipline around the financial engine we have built," CoreWeave said in a statement to Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: India-US trade deal: First phase finalised, legal drafting under way, says Piyush Goyal
articles.summary: The much-awaited India-US trade deal has cleared its first phase and moved to the legal drafting stage, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said
articles.body: The much-awaited India-US trade deal has cleared its first phase and moved to the legal drafting stage, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday.He said that the pact would be operationalised once India gains a competitive advantage over its peer countries. The minister further expressed hope that the process would be completed soon."US bilateral trade agreement's first tranche has been finalised and it is going through final contours, the legal drafting and we hope to be able to finalise that soon and operationalise that once we get the competitive advantage over our peer countries," Goyal said.The minister also provided an update on India's trade negotiations with the European Union, saying that the free trade agreement would be signed in December and is expected to take effect in February or March next year.Earlier in the day, US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor also said that the two nations have cleared the major items on their trade deal checklist. Gor described the pace of negotiations as “incredible.”Gor also spoke about the US legislation that could pave the way for sanctions on countries purchasing Russian oil and gas or helping others evade sanctions. He said US President Donald Trump was expected to decide on the matter within the next 10 days.The legislation received 86 votes in the 100-member US Senate and gives the President the authority to impose sanctions on countries involved in buying Russian oil and gas or facilitating sanctions evasion. Gor said the provisions were not aimed at any particular country, including India.“...We have ongoing discussions on that as it passed with overwhelming bipartisan support. That law got 86 votes out of 100 in our Senate... These sanctions options that Congress passed, they are not targeted at any individual country. It is three different buckets; one is oil, the second is gas, the third is sanctions evasion.”Explaining how countries could fall within the scope of the measures, Gor said their inclusion was based on numbers. He added that India was among several countries that fell into one of the categories, but said the intention was to end the war rather than punish any country.“It just happens that India does fall in one of those buckets, along with a lot of other countries. The goal is not to punish anyone. The goal is to try to bring an end to this war. I do think the president will make a determination on that over the next few days.”Gor said India offered significant opportunities for American businesses, citing the size of its market and the government's approach to foreign investment.India and the US have been negotiating a proposed bilateral trade agreement since early 2025, seeking to address tariff-related tensions, remove non-tariff barriers and improve market access. articles.title: Netflix is slimming down as it gears up for a new streaming battle
articles.summary: Regardless of whether this is AI-related or not, this is a classic strategy of a tech company pivoting to efficiency when it needs a win.
articles.body:
Are you still watching? Apparently, not enough Netflix ( NFLX ) users are answering yes, or bothering to turn the streaming service on at all.

On Wednesday, the industry's leading premium streamer announced it was cutting 6% of its staff, or roughly 1,000 positions , marking Netflix's biggest round of layoffs since 2022, as it copes with a waning audience and a beaten-down stock price. The company's product, HR, tech, and legal departments will be the focus of the cuts, according to an email to employees from co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters.

Netflix has come under pressure from YouTube ( GOOG ) and other media rivals. A year ago, Netflix accounted for 8.8% of all TV viewing time in the US, while YouTube claimed 13.4%, according to Nielsen. This year, Netflix has fallen to 7.8%, with YouTube rising to more than 14%. Even Warren Buffett is watching nightly .

Netflix is also bracing for what a beefed-up Skydance will do , now that the media giant counts both Paramount and Warner Bros. as part of its massive streaming and movie portfolio.

The next era of the streaming wars pits larger, more consolidated companies against each other, even as Hollywood competes with an onslaught of teenagers and young adults who churn out video content for free on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube.

Netflix, like everyone else, is also contending with the AI transition. And that the streamer has reduced headcount mostly in corporate functions is noteworthy. While there's little information about the whys of it all, our minds went immediately to AI's productivity potential, hitting the administrative side of the entertainment industry.

If that's the case, it would be an ironic turn for Hollywood, with its high-profile AI debate hinging mostly on writers and actors. Though many creatives have loudly opposed the use of AI in their processes, entertainment companies may be more willing to deploy tools in other departments, just like the rest of the more tech-savvy players in corporate America.

Regardless of whether this is AI or not — and we will know more when the company reports on Tuesday — this is a classic strategy of pivoting to efficiency and cost when margin needs to be found somewhere.

Shares initially rose on the layoff announcement before reversing to virtually unchanged.

Hamza Shaban is a reporter for Yahoo Finance covering markets and the economy. Follow Hamza on X @hshaban .

articles.title: At its New York design studio, Walmart bets on affordable, trendy clothes
articles.summary: Walmart's investment in private-label brands comes as many consumers, feeling the pressure from rising living costs, carefully weigh discretionary purchases.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — On the fifth floor of an unassuming building in Manhattan, Walmart's New York City fashion office buzzes with activity as the low-cost retailer pushes for recognition in one of the style capitals of the world.

The minimalist office, formerly occupied by menswear brand Bonobos, is where Walmart ( WMT ) designs apparel for its private-label brands Scoop, Free Assembly, and Scenario as part of a bet to attract the deeper wallets of higher-income customers.

There, roughly 160 Walmart employees across brand, design, fit, and style teams work to create $60 cashmere sweaters and other trendy items that the company hopes inspire people to ask, "That's from Walmart?!"

"We made a real intentional choice to say that we wanted to move forward even more in our fashion," Walmart US executive vice president and chief merchandising officer Julie Barber told Yahoo Finance. "The majority of our team sits in Bentonville. They're doing the buying, but we needed a select group of people here in New York closer to some of the trends and things that were happening."

The investment in private-label brands comes as many consumers, feeling the pressure from rising living costs, carefully weigh discretionary purchases . At the same time, Walmart competitors Amazon ( AMZN ) and Costco ( COST ) have carved out a space in the apparel market.

"I do think that Amazon and Costco have, in a way, paved the way for someone like Walmart to see a vision where customers can be thinking about buying apparel kind of from the same place that they're buying ketchup and laundry detergent," David Silverman, senior director at Fitch Ratings, told Yahoo Finance.

Slowing sales present yet another reason for Walmart to become a one-stop shop for design and essentials. In the second quarter, the company posted its slowest US same-store sales growth since Q4 of 2020, at 2.6%.

Grocery still accounts for the majority of Walmart's US sales; however, general merchandise, including apparel, represents a growing part of the business, and the percentage of sales coming from private-label brands increased by 1.3 percentage points year over year.

"There is … an opportunity to cover more higher-income shoppers who recently came in for grocery to cross the aisle to fashion," said Neil Saunders, managing director of GlobalData.

From grocery staples to New York Fashion Week

Walmart has been quietly building out its fashion strategy for years with the goal of getting shoppers, especially the high-income shoppers it gained in recent years, to spend more.

articles.title: An industry is prescribing weight-loss drugs to people with anorexia, devastating lives
articles.summary: For AJ Jasper, drugs hailed as miracles have proven nothing short of a curse.
articles.body: For AJ Jasper, drugs hailed as miracles have proven nothing short of a curse. In 2024, a hard-won truce between Jasper and the anorexia he had battled, on and off, since childhood collapsed, sending him spiraling to his lowest ebb yet. He was only a few pounds below his target weight, but a stressful period compelled Jasper to seek out a new, revolutionary class of weight-loss medication. Jasper said he submitted a form to the telehealth site Hims & Hers, lying about his weight and asking for a GLP-1 prescription. He expected to speak to a doctor. For there to be more questions. Yet in about two days, the medication was at his door. “I thought that there would be roadblocks,” he told CNN from his apartment in Chicago. CNN spoke to several clinicians and eating disorder specialists reporting sharp rises in the numbers of patients with anorexia using GLP-1s, many of whom obtained them via telehealth platforms with remarkable ease. Millions of people worldwide are using the drugs to lose weight, but their omnipresence has made it difficult for some people who have anorexia to recover or to remain in recovery. Globally, about 3.9 million people have anorexia nervosa — a complex mental health and eating disorder in which people severely restrict their energy intake to lose weight — according to the latest estimates from 2023 by the University of Washington-based Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation. A study of 436 adults with eating disorders, published in June by the University of Louisville and research institute RTI International, found that a little over 20% of those currently diagnosed with anorexia reported ever having used a GLP-1 — higher than the 15% of US adults who report using the drug at some point for weight loss. Jasper, 40, has sought treatment and stabilized and relapsed several times in the past two years. He has purchased the drugs from a number of telehealth sites, including Ro, Good Life Meds, MEDVi and Priority Meds, sometimes taking several simultaneously to maximize the effect. He’s only ever used compounded, copycat versions of name-brand drugs, as they are cheaper and come in vials rather than pre-filled pens — meaning he could administer many times the recommended dose. The nadir came in January, when Jasper’s treatment team insisted that he check into a hospital. A friend took Jasper, who, bed-bound, had become so malnourished and so underweight that he could hardly lift his head and his heart, liver and kidneys had begun to fail. “I was completely depleted,” he said. Throughout the nightmare, Jasper knew he could easily obtain what he describes as “anorexic heroin” and drop weight at a bewildering scale and speed. If one site made buying GLP-1s harder by requiring a video consultation with a clinician, he could simply use another. If a request form asked him about a history of eating disorders, he could tick “no,” and a confirmation email — arriving often within 24 hours — would inform him that the medication was already on its way. Complex rules Rules governing telehealth sites in the United States are complicated and vary state by state. All require a clinician to establish a relationship with a patient before prescribing, which can happen via a real-time video or phone call, a previous in-person meeting or through a less immediate method, like a questionnaire. Most states do not, however, allow the latter to be the sole basis of this relationship, according to the Center for Connected Health Policy. Illinois, where Jasper lives, requires, for example, optometrists to conduct in-person visits to establish a patient connection, but its rules are less explicit about how to do so for a raft of other specialties and prescription types, according to the CCHP. A spokesperson for Hims & Hers said that screening for eating disorders is a mandatory part of its prescribing process and that, as with in-person appointments, clinicians require patients to be honest about their health history. “Any answer indicating current or past disordered eating triggers additional clinical questions, closer provider review, and in many cases a referral to specialty eating disorder care off our platform,” the spokesperson said. A spokesperson for Ro said that it asks all patients to complete an intake form including questions about eating disorders. Clinicians use these details “to evaluate treatment eligibility and can, at any point, request records, require a video evaluation, or order lab testing to further understand a patient’s health,” the spokesperson said, adding that patients with a history of eating disorders are directed to “seek in-person care.” Both platforms said they regularly follow up with patients to spot problems during treatment. Jasper said he ignored any check-in emails. Telehealth platform RXPros acquired PriorityMeds earlier this year. “Patient safety and appropriate clinical oversight were central to (PriorityMeds’) processes,” a spokesperson for RXPros told CNN. MEDVi and Good Life Meds did not respond to requests for comment. Jasper has made huge leaps in recovery since January. He doesn’t want to demonize drugs that he knows are helping scores of people become healthier, nor does he want his story to be another cautionary tale. But he does want more guardrails around telehealth platforms. ‘Prescription is lax’ The Princeton Center for Eating Disorders once treated only the most severe cases of anorexia that require round-the-clock care. But the New Jersey treatment center recently introduced a program allowing patients to return home for the evening, offering more autonomy. “GLP-1 medication use has, already, in the three months this program has been open, been a major interfering factor in treatment for multiple patients,” said its director, Rebecca Boswell. She spoke of instances where patients were prescribed GLP-1s by physicians — working independently of telehealth platforms — after an in-person appointment and when an anorexia diagnosis had been well-established. Physicians uninformed about the condition have often agreed with a patient’s belief that silencing their “food noise” will help, she said. In other cases, Boswell’s patients have bought GLP-1s via telehealth sites without ever meeting a physician. Telehealth sites hit their first jackpot in the 2010s, when Viagra and other drugs for erectile dysfunction came off patent, allowing for the sale of cheaper generics. They hit another jackpot in the early 2020s, when staggering demand for GLP-1s made by pharmaceutical titans Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk led to a global shortage and regulators in the United States temporarily permitted telehealth companies to sell compounded versions. The industry as a whole has grown rapidly over the past decade and is built on the demand for drugs targeting common conditions — and that can be accessed discreetly — such as hair loss treatments and hormone replacement therapies. During the pandemic, a relaxation of some rules governing online prescribing in the US gave companies an additional boost. But the GLP-1 opportunity “kind of came out of nowhere and no one really expected it to get this big,” said Brian Tanquilut, a senior equity analyst covering the healthcare sector at investment firm Jefferies. Some company business models are based on selling high volumes of a product, he said, making a smooth pathway to prescription necessary. “Prescription is lax,” he noted of GLP-1s, which aren’t classed as “controlled substances” by the US government — those carrying a risk of addiction or abuse — and thus less strictly regulated. “Anyone who wants it can get it, for the most part.” Last year, researchers at Yale tested that impression, creating a fake profile that attempted to obtain a GLP-1 prescription through 49 different websites. The “secret shopper” study found that 92% of websites ultimately prescribed the drugs, only 55% asked about a history of eating disorders, and 33% mandated either a video or phone call with a clinician. On average, prescriptions were issued within a day. Two were issued in five minutes or less. Researchers said the results indicated that some websites were prioritizing “quick prescriptions over comprehensive care.” Regulators are just beginning to clamp down on the industry from several angles: for rampant compounding and misleading advertising in the United States, to permissive and potentially unsafe prescribing in Australia, Britain and India. Kerri Fleming, head of service development at Beat, a British eating disorder charity, said telehealth providers often ask patients to upload photos to help verify their weight. She said some sites have introduced a “live photo” system to prevent abuse. According to Fleming, some people with anorexia have falsified their image using artificial intelligence or by submitting one of a friend or family member instead. “The clinicians that work (for many telehealth sites) are very much aware of the risks and are trying to improve practices continuously,” she said. “It’s just an ever-changing landscape that is a hard one to navigate.” Kyle Zebley, chief executive officer of the American Telemedicine Association, said the risk of misprescribing is the same across virtual and face-to-face settings when patients are trusted to report on their own problems. “A questionnaire that can be gamed with false information is a clinical governance failure, not a telehealth-specific one,” Zebley said in a statement, adding that the ATA supports “rigorous enforcement against any company or clinician cutting corners on patient safety.” A spokesperson for Eli Lilly told CNN that telehealth providers prescribing its GLP-1 medications – including Mounjaro and Zepbound – operate independently and that “they use their own clinical judgement when treating patients.” Lilly “does not promote or encourage” the use of its drugs for unapproved conditions, the spokesperson said. Mette Kruse Danielsen, a communications director for Novo Nordisk, the maker of Ozempic and Wegovy, said patient safety is a “top priority” for the company and that its products are “not approved for the treatment of eating disorders.” Pervasive use Anorexia has one of highest mortality rates of any psychiatric disorder, and clinicians told CNN that frequent GLP-1 use among patients as well as the drug’s cultural ubiquity are changing approaches to treatment. They are “part of every conversation” Tom Hildebrandt is having with anorexia patients in his clinic at the Icahn School of Medicine at New York City’s Mount Sinai, many of whom report feeling encircled by family and friends taking the drugs. One patient, he said, was offered a GLP-1 at a party. Some patients seek out GLP-1s to quiet their “food noise,” Hildebrandt said. And while there is emerging evidence that the drugs could be an effective treatment for some people with binge eating disorder or bulimia, clinicians interviewed by CNN were unanimous in their rejection of any purported therapeutic benefit for anorexia. When the body is starving, the brain will return an incessant and often distressing loop of thoughts about food, an adaptive response designed to prioritize renourishment that clinicians try to harness rather than shut down. Jasper, in Chicago, understands the risk of silencing those hunger cues. He described himself as a “walking calculator” during periods of struggle with anorexia before taking GLP-1s, incessantly tracking calories ingested and expended. But he said the drugs turned him into a “zombie.” The food obsessions, fears and even nightmares went away, but so too did Jasper’s grasp of the seriousness of his condition. “(I wasn’t) even able to fully comprehend that I was actively dying. … With the medication, I was never able to realize how malnourished I was because I wasn’t thinking about food at all,” he said. He has created a petition he hopes will attract the attention of lawmakers, urging the introduction of new safeguards around online prescribing. “It’s the wild, wild West,” said Jasper.

articles.title: Fed's Goolsbee: Even without AI, the economy would not be in recession
articles.summary: Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee argues that the AI boom isn't simply adding to economic growth; it is actively cannibalizing resources from...
articles.body:
As artificial intelligence develops at a blistering pace, boosting parts of the economy, both industry leaders and watchdogs argue it should be slowed down to ensure the technology is developed safely.

But what would that mean for economic growth? Would the economy be as strong without AI?

Chicago Federal Reserve president Austan Goolsbee argues that the AI boom isn't simply adding to economic growth; it is actively cannibalizing resources from other traditional industries.

"You can't just look at the rest of the economy and say that's how it would be doing if the AI build-out wasn't there," Goolsbee said in an interview with Yahoo Finance. "Part of why I haven't thought until recently that AI was overheating the aggregate economy is that it's kind of uncomfortably shoving down other sectors."

Goolsbee said he's seeing this play out in his Midwestern district, where local businesses are increasingly complaining about skyrocketing costs, driven directly by intense competition with tech giants.

"A lot of it is we're in competition for the same resources, the same electricians, the same components, the same land, the same construction," Goolsbee said.

Since AI's rise has suppressed other sectors, the aggregate economy has managed to avoid boiling over. A sudden slowdown in AI wouldn't automatically trigger a recession, Goolsbee said, because if tech demand were to cool, it could simply release pent-up capacity and allow sidelined industries to recover.

However, Goolsbee warned that the velocity of the AI build-out is starting to boost growth more widely.

"The growth has been so rapid that now you're starting to see a retightening of the labor market," Goolsbee cautioned. "Now it becomes more of a concern of just the old-fashioned overheated demand kind of variety."

Jennifer Schonberger is a veteran financial journalist covering markets, the economy, and investing. At Yahoo Finance, she covers the Federal Reserve, Congress, the White House, the Treasury, the SEC, the economy, cryptocurrencies, and the intersection of Washington policy with finance. Follow her on X @Jenniferisms and on Instagram .

articles.title: No more guessing who's calling! Govt mandates caller ID display from November 1
articles.summary: Unknown calls bothering you? The name behind it will no longer be a secret.
articles.body: Unknown calls bothering you? The name behind it will no longer be a secret.The department of telecommunications (DoT) has directed telecom operators to introduce Calling Name Presentation (CNAP) from November 1, 2026. The service will display the caller’s name on the recipient’s phone without requiring users to sign up separately. It will initially be available on 4G and higher-generation networks, while its rollout on 2G, 3G and landline networks will be considered separately.When a call comes in, the recipient’s screen will show the caller’s number along with their name. If the number is saved in the recipient’s contacts, the name stored there will appear on the screen. While for an unsaved domestic number, the name recorded in the caller’s telecom operator’s subscriber records will be displayed.International calls will be handled differently. If the number is not saved in the recipient’s contacts, the screen will display ‘International Call’ instead of the caller’s name. This applies to calls between two countries where either India or the other country is the point of origin or destination.How will telecom operators identify callers?The system will rely on a database maintained by the telecom operator from which the call originates. Each operator will have to establish, operate and maintain a database linking the calling name identity of its users with their assigned telecommunication identifiers.When a call reaches the recipient’s network, the terminating telecom service provider will retrieve the relevant name from this database and display it to the recipient.The DoT’s instructions apply to all telecom service providers holding authorisation or licences to provide access services. The department has directed them to implement the service across their respective service areas from November 1, 2026.Will names of all callers be displayed?The rules provide an exception for users who have opted for the calling line identification restriction (CLIR) facility in accordance with existing guidelines. The calling name identity of these users will not be displayed.For other callers, the name displayed will depend on whether their number is saved in the recipient’s contacts and, if it is not, the applicable rules for domestic and international calls.The instructions also allow telecom operators to offer a separate facility to businesses and users with bulk connections to display a preferred name instead of the name recorded in their subscriber data records.Businesses can use registered trade namesBusinesses opting for a preferred name will have to meet verification requirements. The name must either be a trademark registered in the user’s name with the trade marks registry under the controller general of patents, designs and trade marks, department for promotion of industry and internal trade, ministry of commerce and industry, or a trade name registered on the Goods and Services Tax portal.For new connections, the preferred name must be recorded in both the customer application form and the subscriber data record. Applicants must present original documents establishing registration under the proposed name. The telecom operator will attach true copies of these documents to the customer application form.For existing connections, operators must establish a mechanism through which businesses can apply to have their preferred names recorded. The name may be updated in the subscriber data record after the application has been examined and properly verified.Telecom operators must also carry out due diligence and retain a true copy of the documents proving registration under the preferred name after checking them against the originals.Data retention and security safeguardsThe DoT has prescribed safeguards to protect communications and ensure that the introduction of the service does not affect the quality of telecom services.Operators must follow a security-by-design approach, under which the query-response mechanism itself must ensure that the calling name identity is not retained after the incoming call is completed.They must also ensure that their databases, networks and connectivity infrastructure can handle calling name identity queries efficiently and retrieve and deliver the information in a timely manner. The quality of telecommunication services must be maintained in accordance with applicable laws.Users will also have a grievance redressal mechanism for complaints related to the service. Every telecom service provider must put in place appropriate technical and organisational measures to receive, record and maintain such grievances, and address them within a specified timeframe. The Central Government may issue further instructions and clarifications as required.The DoT’s instructions refer to the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India’s (TRAI) recommendations on introducing Calling Name Presentation in Indian telecom networks, dated February 23, 2024. They also refer to the department’s instructions dated November 21, 2025, concerning the handling of know-your-customer (KYC) issues during implementation of the service.You use AI every day. articles.title: She bought shares for Rs 13.5 lakh and sold them for Rs 77.47 lakh after 18 months; taxman denied capital gains exemption, but ITAT gives relief and deletes Rs 79 lakh in additions
articles.summary: You buy shares in a company and after over a year you sell them. In between the company also issues bonus shares, taking your total holdings up.
articles.body: You buy shares in a company and after over a year you sell them. In between the company also issues bonus shares, taking your total holdings up. You claim the proceeds from the sale under capital gains tax exemption, but the Income Tax Department rejects your claim. What do you do?In one such case, the Mumbai bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) has deleted additions of around Rs 79 lakh made in connection with the sale of shares.The case concerned a woman who claimed an exemption on long-term capital gains of Rs 65.41 lakh from the sale of shares.What the case is aboutA woman purchased 60,000 shares of a company Ltd between March 3 and March 15, 2011, for Rs 13,52,850, at Rs 22.55 per share. The company subsequently issued bonus shares in a 1:1 ratio, which increased her holding to 1.2 lakh shares.Also Read | Wife sold shares for Rs 8.31 crore LTCG, bought husband’s Mumbai property for Rs 7.5 crore and claimed Section 54F exemption; taxman calls it tax avoidance, but ITAT Mumbai gives relief to herThe woman sold the shares between August 31 and December 24, 2012, and got around Rs 77,47,600. The transactions were conducted through the Bombay Stock Exchange's online platform, routed through banking channels and subjected to securities transaction tax (STT).She claimed long-term capital gains of Rs 65,41,902 as exempt under Section 10(38) of the Income Tax Act.However, the assessing officer rejected her exemption claim and treated the full sale consideration as unexplained. A separate addition of Rs 1,54,952 was also made under Section 69C towards alleged commission expenditure.The case involved shares of a company which had also featured in other tax disputes involving allegations of price manipulation and bogus transactions.The National Faceless Appeal Centre upheld the additions, following which the woman then appealed against it at ITAT.The records she had submitted to the lower authorities included share purchase and sale contract notes, bank statements, demat account statements and evidence of the sale proceeds received from the broker.She also provided information from the official websites of the Bombay Stock Exchange and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs showing the company's status.Also Read | Taxpayer declared Rs 1.79 lakh in ITR, faced Rs 11.22 crore income addition on large cash deposits, unsecured loans; ITAT grants him chance to substantiate case with condition he plant 500 treesWhy did the woman get relief from ITAT?The central issue before the ITAT was whether the transactions could be treated as bogus when the investor had furnished documents tracing the purchase, holding and sale of the shares, but the Income Tax Department had not established her involvement in the alleged manipulation.The tribunal noted that the lower authorities had not found the documents to be false or fabricated. It also found no material establishing that the woman was involved in price rigging or manipulation of the shares.In its order, ITAT observed that the evidence relating to the purchase, holding and sale of the shares had not been disproved by the department. It added that no material had been produced to establish a connection between the woman and alleged manipulation or accommodation-entry providers.The tribunal stated: “no material has been brought on record to establish any nexus of the Assessee with the alleged manipulation or accommodation-entry providers.”Also Read | Homebuyer got parking from builder in 2008, but society later adopted a 'first come, first served' rule; Maharashtra court protects resident's space until ownership dispute is decidedIt also noted that the shares had been held for more than one-and-a-half years, the transactions had taken place through banking channels, and the sales were executed through a recognised stock exchange. The bench further observed that no allegation of manipulation, rigging or collusion with the promoters or any other person had been proved against the woman.The tribunal relied on earlier decisions involving similar allegations and the same company's shares in which the Mumbai ITAT had deleted additions involving the same scrip. It also referred to the Bombay High Court's decision in PCIT-31 vs. Indravadan Jain, HUF, concerning share transactions supported by contract notes, demat records and banking evidence, where the investor's involvement in alleged price manipulation had not been established.Considering the documents, the absence of evidence linking the woman to manipulation and the judicial precedents, the tribunal held that the additions could not be sustained.It therefore deleted the Rs 77,47,600 addition which was for the entire sale consideration after rejecting the exemption claim, along with the separate Rs 1,54,952 addition towards alleged commission expenditure. The order was pronounced on September 8, 2026, and the appeal was allowed.Akhil Chandna, Partner and Global People Solutions Leader, Grant Thornton Bharat explains that what weighed in the taxpayer’s favour was that the department could not point to anything showing her involvement in the alleged manipulation of share prices.“The taxpayer had submitted the purchase and sale details, contract notes, demat statements and bank records. These were not found to be false or fabricated. The ITAT also took into account earlier rulings involving the same company’s shares, where additions made on similar grounds had been deleted,” Chandna tells TOI.Also Read | Man enters JDA for land, gets 6 flats from builder and transfers 5 to wife, but gets tax notice; ITAT Delhi deletes Rs 4.14 crore additions after finding no stock-in-trade conversion or saleSignificance of rulingAccording to Chandna, the decision makes an important distinction: A sharp rise in the price of a share may raise questions, but that alone cannot be the basis for rejecting a taxpayer’s claim of exempt long-term capital gains. There must be some evidence connecting the taxpayer with the alleged manipulation.“For taxpayers, especially those dealing in low-priced shares, retaining the complete transaction records is important. However, such records may not be sufficient where the department has evidence linking the taxpayer to the alleged manipulation,” he says.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Why CoreWeave stock panic matters to Nvidia, explained in under 30 seconds
articles.summary: Nvidia can't ignore CRWV's market troubles.
articles.body:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang is unlikely to ignore the building pressure on CoreWeave's ( CRWV ) stock price and bond values.

The simple reason why is that he can't look the other way given how intertwined Nvidia is with the most well-known — and debated — neocloud.

For one, in January of this year Nvidia announced an expansion of its relationship with CoreWeave. The deal included Nvidia investing $2 billion in CoreWeave stock. CoreWeave committed to using Nvidia's technology to build more than 5 gigawatts of AI factories by 2030.

Nvidia now holds 47.2 million shares of CoreWeave stock, or around 10% of the company.

And two, CoreWeave is a huge customer of Nvidia, as seen below in the chart from the team at Boring Business.

CoreWeave buys GPUs from Nvidia and then rents that compute back to other companies, including the hyperscalers like Meta ( META ).

"0% chance $NVDA lets $CRWV falter," said tech analyst Daniel Newman on X .

Yet, failure of CoreWeave is what the market is chatting about.

Shares of CoreWeave plunged 6% in pre-market trading on Thursday following a 15% rout on Wednesday.

"In our view, the company's long-term business model remains economically challenged; we maintain our Underperform," Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei said in a note Thursday.

Two factors collided to spark Wednesday's sell-off.

One, CoreWeave's corporate bonds across maturities continued to be dumped on fears of an AI slowdown and what that would mean for the company's precarious balance sheet.

The rise in yields on CoreWeave's bonds even spurred Elon Musk to post "Yikes" on X in response to a post by venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya.

Two, Gartner, in a new report, forecast that by 2030 "cost pressure and a lack of a differentiating business model will force over 80% of neocloud providers to cease independent operations."

CoreWeave is a neocloud. The report essentially was akin to yelling fire in a crowded theater.

At some point soon, Huang may have to step in and comment on Nvidia's confidence in CoreWeave. He has a financial interest in doing so not only from an Nvidia standpoint, but also from the viewpoint of the wider AIm boom his chips are fueling.

articles.title: India’s September exports rise 23% as merchandise trade deficit narrows; shipments to US rise 11%
articles.summary: India's merchandise exports rose 23.04% year-on-year to $44.40 billion in September 2026, up from $36.08 billion a year earlier, according to data
articles.body: India's merchandise exports rose 23.04% year-on-year to $44.40 billion in September 2026, up from $36.08 billion a year earlier, according to data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Thursday.The merchandise trade deficit narrowed to $30.21 billion from $33 billion in September last year, even as imports increased to $74.61 billion from $69.08 billion, the data showed.India's overall exports, including merchandise and services, grew 10.99% to an estimated $80.75 billion in September, compared with $72.76 billion a year earlier.Overall imports rose to $94.05 billion from $86.93 billion, while the combined trade deficit narrowed to $13.30 billion from $14.17 billion, according to the ministry.Electronics, engineering goods drive export growthCommerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal said merchandise shipments were driving the growth in exports."If you look at merchandise exports in September, they are at $44.40 billion, which is 23.04 per cent higher than last September," he said during a press briefing, according to news agency ANI.Higher shipments of electronic goods, petroleum products, engineering goods, chemicals and agricultural products supported the increase.Agrawal also said export growth had accelerated in the second quarter of the current financial year. Overall exports grew 15.84% in July-September, compared with 11.84% in the first quarter, he said.According to the ministry's presentation, India's overall exports reached an estimated $242.6 billion in the second quarter, compared with $233.6 billion in April-June. The July-September figure was the highest ever recorded for the second quarter.Imports rise as merchandise trade gap narrowsMerchandise imports increased to $74.61 billion in September from $70.67 billion in August, while exports rose from $43.81 billion to $44.40 billion over the same period, according to government data.The merchandise trade deficit stood at $30.21 billion, marginally below economists' expectations of $30.4 billion in a Reuters poll. However, it was higher than the $26.86 billion deficit recorded in August.Global energy prices remain a factor in India's import bill. Brent crude futures have stayed above $100 a barrel amid the Iran war, while attacks around the Strait of Hormuz have increased.Iran has said it is stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.India looks to expand export marketsIndia is seeking to diversify its export markets through trade agreements with key partners. A trade deal with New Zealand is set to take effect next week, while India's trade pact with Britain is already in force. A broader agreement with the European Union is moving towards implementation.The United States remained India's largest merchandise export destination in the first half of the current financial year, despite tariff-related disruptions.India's merchandise exports to the US rose 11.1% to $50.81 billion during April-September 2026, compared with $45.73 billion a year earlier.Imports from the US increased 26% to $32.33 billion from $25.66 billion, according to data presented by the commerce ministry.India's merchandise trade surplus with the US narrowed to $18.48 billion from $20.07 billion in the corresponding period last year.Agrawal said negotiations for the proposed India-US trade agreement were progressing in the right direction, with both sides working towards concluding the deal at the earliest."The negotiations are in the right direction. Probably, we are in a very good zone. We anticipate closing the deal and signing it at the earliest possible time," he said.He said the agreement would depend on the finalisation of the broader US tariff framework, with a parallel process underway under Section 301."The deal has to be signed when the overall tariff structure is getting formalised. There is parallel work being done in the US also to get back the tariff structure based on some of the outcomes of the 301," he said.Agrawal added that India was seeking preferential access to the US market to help its exporters compete with those from other countries."When you do a trade deal, it gives you not only market access in each other's markets; it gives you preferential market access in a particular market," he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: PNC Third-Quarter Lending Revenue Misses Estimates as Costs Beat
articles.summary: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. reported third-quarter revenue that missed analysts’ estimates while the bank did a better job of keeping expenses in check...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- PNC Financial Services Group Inc. reported third-quarter revenue that missed analysts' estimates while the bank did a better job of keeping expenses in check than expected.

Non-interest expenses of $3.75 billion beat the $3.77 billion average estimate of analysts surveyed by Bloomberg, while revenue of $6.56 billion compared with the $6.58 billion estimate for total income from interest and fees.

Higher interest rates cut both ways for net interest income, what the bank earns on loans and securities minus funding costs. While commercial loans increased at the Pittsburgh-based company, especially after the acquisition of FirstBank Holding Co. in January, and other interest-earning assets generated higher yields, funding costs also increased, according to a statement Thursday.

PNC's bigger rivals, which reported results earlier this week, offered an optimistic outlook for 2027, assuming further rate hikes will fuel already strong growth in NII. JPMorgan Chase & Co. forecast a 10% increase in NII next year, excluding trading activities, and Bank of America Corp. expects NII to be 8% higher than this year.

Net interest income at PNC rose 2.4% from the second quarter to $4.21 billion. That fell short of the consensus estimate of $4.23 billion.

"Our strategy continues to drive growth across our businesses, as we deepen our presence in key markets and expand our reach nationally," Chief Executive Officer Bill Demchak said in the statement.

For regional banks, investors are eager to see if the bond-market selloff since August will resurface the issue of paper losses on their securities portfolios. That was at the center of industry turmoil in 2023, making banks vulnerable to deposit outflows and constraining their ability to deploy capital.

PNC got a head start on reducing paper losses in the second quarter, selling some securities at a loss and taking a one-time $139 million charge. In the third quarter, its average investment securities rose to $151.4 billion, up 3% from the prior quarter. The increase resulted from the bank's decision to buy more residential mortgage-backed securities, according to the statement.

articles.title: Global tech selloff deepens as enthusiasm for AI stocks wobbles
articles.summary: Global technology stocks sold off sharply Thursday, as a growing list of worries, including rising borrowing costs and tougher competition from China, caused traders to sour on AI investments.
articles.body: Global technology stocks sold off sharply Thursday, as a growing list of worries, including rising borrowing costs and tougher competition from China, caused traders to sour on AI investments. Nasdaq futures were down 1.1% shortly after 6.30 a E.T. The tech-heavy index posted its worst decline since July on Wednesday, as shares of companies involved in the AI buildout, including chipmakers, tumbled. CoreWeave, a data center provider backed by Nvidia, fell 6% in premarket trading, after plunging 15.5% Wednesday. Oracle fell more than 2% premarket, having closed nearly 9% lower Wednesday. Intel, SpaceX and Nvidia were also poised to open sharply lower. “Worries about the AI buildout, bubbly valuations, lower-than-expected earnings growth at leading US frontier labs, Chinese competition, inflation and rates sent investors running for the covers,” Neil Wilson, a strategist at investment bank Saxo wrote in a note. He pointed to the slowing pace of revenue growth at Anthropic and OpenAI as adding to investor concerns. Multiple news outlets reported that Anthropic, at an investor presentation ahead of its planned IPO expected in the near future, announced its sales grew 45% to $17 billion last quarter. Growth had more than doubled in the second quarter. Further hitting sentiment, C.C. Wei, the CEO of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world’s largest manufacturer of advanced chips, sounded a cautious note during an earnings call Thursday. He told analysts that rising component prices and macroeconomic uncertainty was challenging demand in some segments of the market. The company’s shares finished 2% lower despite bumper earnings, contributing to a 3.5% decline in an index of Taiwan’s technology stocks. South Korea’s Kospi led declines in Asia, finishing 7.6% lower on sharp drops in chipmakers SK Hynix (-11%) and Samsung Electronics (-9.5%). The scale of the decline triggered a circuit breaker, temporarily halting trading on the exchange – a frequent occurrence this year in a stock market dominated by just two stocks. Japan’s Nikkei finished 4.9% lower, with Hong Kong’s Hang Seng down 1%. An index of technology stocks in Europe fell 3% in early afternoon trade locally, with Dutch semiconductor manufacturer ASML down nearly 5%. The global retreat in technology stocks followed a sharp selloff overnight on Wall Street, after a strong US inflation print bolstered worries that rising interest rates will make it more expensive for companies to fund AI investments. Many AI companies are already heavily indebted. “A slowdown in the AI infrastructure build out would imply a sharp slowdown in US growth expectations,” Mohit Kumar, chief European economist at Jefferies said in a note. The US is spending more on AI annually as a percentage of GDP than it did on building railways across the country in the 1800s, he noted. AI stock valuations have been volatile throughout the year. The biggest hyperscalers – Anthropic and OpenAI – remain privately traded, so investors look for clues about AI demand elsewhere. One report that hints about slumping demand or higher-than-expected costs of building out AI infrastructure has frequently sent stocks on a rollercoaster ride. But fears of a bubble suddenly popping have tended to be overblown. “We expect the earnings season to justify that earnings and demand remain robust,” Kumar added. He cautioned, however, that Jefferies “would look to take some chips off the table” ahead of the midterms because a potential Democrat win in Congress “would be considered negative for the sector.” Adding to market jitters is growing competitive pressure from China, after Chinese semiconductor CXMT announced progress on advanced memory chips, raising doubts about the potential profitability of companies in the US and South Korea.

articles.title: TSMC posts record profit amid 'extremely robust demand' for AI chips
articles.summary: TSMC reported quarterly revenue as investors look for clues about the health of the AI trade.
articles.body:
What happened: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company ( TSM ) stock was poised to open lower on Thursday despite posting a record profit and beating estimates amid global demand for AI chips.

What's behind the move: TSMC reported a sixth straight quarter of record profits as the company's bottom line jumped nearly 69% while revenue surged 51%.

The Taiwan-based contract chip manufacturer's sales are expected to reach as much as $54.3 billion for its current quarter, beating analyst estimates.

"Demand for our leading-edge technologies continue to be extremely robust," TSMC CEO C.C. Wei said during the call. "We observe increasing AI demand fueled by the rising adoption of agentic AI as we transition from chatbot to AI assistance."

Third-quarter gross margin was 66.4%, down from 67.7% in the second quarter. TSMC expects gross margin of 65% to 67% for the fourth quarter.

"Given the continued robust multi-year demand from our customers, including the emerging agentic AI market, we reiterate our full-year 2026 capital budget to be between $60 billion and $64 billion," said TSMC's CFO Wendell Huang.

The company expects capex from 2026 to 2028 "to be even more significantly higher than the past three years," as it continues to invest heavily to support customers' growth, added Huang.

What else you need to know: The company is closely tied to the AI infrastructure buildout and its execution, as it manufactures advanced processors designed by chip giants such as Nvidia ( NVDA ), AMD ( AMD ), and Broadcom ( AVGO ).

TSMC stock is up more than 41% year to date as of Wednesday's close. Shares reached all-time highs earlier this month after Tesla ( TSLA ) and SpaceX ( SPCX ) CEO Elon Musk acknowledged early-stage talks with the world's largest chip foundry about a potential collaboration on his Terafab semiconductor initiative in Texas.

TSMC, which is already undergoing significant expansion in Arizona as part of a multi-year plan to manufacture chips stateside for its clients, confirmed it is exploring Texas.

"We send the teams to Texas to do all the evaluation," CEO C.C. Wei said during the call. "We also talk to one of our customer who try to build a fab, Terafab, let me be more specific."

Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.
